item.title: WZIP and WLZ4: LZ77 Codecs with Match-Length-Dependent Sliding Windows
item.description: arXiv:2610.14079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An LZ77 codec bounds every match by one sliding window, trading cheap offsets for short matches against reach for long ones. Match-length-dependent windows refine this trade-off: each match length has its own window, and the decoder infers the offset range from the decoded length. We present two such codecs: WLZ4, a byte-aligned LZ4-class format with one-byte and flagged offsets, and WZIP, an entropy-coded Zstandard-class format. Each block begins with its decoded length, from which WZIP derives its widest window and a decoder sizes its output. LZ4 blocks may expand incompressible input by 0.4%; WLZ4 adds at most 15 bytes, WZIP 2. We describe the formats, threaded match finders, decoders and parser. On Silesia, WLZ4 reaches a ratio up to 16% above LZ4HC's, decoding more slowly, and WZIP exceeds Zstandard 22's ratio while its trusted decoder runs at 91% of Zstandard's speed (87% checked; on enwik9, about as fast).
item.dc:creator: Yingquan "Cody" Wu

item.title: The weight enumerators of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the spectral relation between irreducible cyclic codes (ICC) and generalized Paley (GP) graphs recently found by the authors, we study the weight distribution of irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$, $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. These codes were previously studied by Sharma, Bakshi and Raka, who divided them into two families (each having two cases). First we characterize the GP-graphs spectrally related to these families of ICCs: they are complete, semiprimitive, Hamming, or Cartesian products of semiprimitive GP-graphs. We then compute the spectrum of these graphs and hence, by the mentioned spectral relation we finally obtain neat explicit expressions for the weight enumerators of all the irreducible cyclic codes of length $2^\ell$ with $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo A. Podest\'a, Denis E. Videla

item.title: Quantum Annealing for Resource Allocation in Next-Generation Wireless Communication Networks: A QUBO Modeling Guide
item.description: arXiv:2610.14126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum annealing (QA) offers a physics-inspired approach for such subproblems by mapping them onto an Ising Hamiltonian, which is algebraically equivalent to a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model executable on quantum annealers or hybrid solvers. However, their practical employment in wireless systems critically depends on the specific problem formulation, on the particular variable encoding, constraint handling, solver selection, hardware embedding, and fair benchmarking. This paper develops wireless-oriented QUBO modeling guidelines for QA-assisted resource allocation. We first present a beginner-friendly toy example in which a terrestrial-aerial resource-allocation problem with a fractional signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) maximization objective is reformulated into a two-bit QUBO via Boolean interpolation, converted into an Ising representation, and decoded back into a wireless scheduling decision. The same scheduling is applicable to UAV, aircraft, satellite, and terrestrial links in SAGIN systems. We then review the QA foundations and solver ecosystems, including binary quadratic, discrete quadratic, constrained quadratic, and hybrid models from the perspective of NG wireless optimization. Furthermore, we discuss both binary and discrete encoding, penalty-based constraint conversion, embedding overhead, solution decoding, and feasibility verification. A QUBO Compatibility Index is introduced as a lightweight diagnostic metric for assessing the associated QUBO formulation readiness, rather than a predictor of runtime or solution quality. Finally, a case study on max-min uplink power control in cell-free massive MIMO illustrates how a fairness-oriented wireless problem can be discretized, constrained, converted into the concept of a QUBO, and evaluated against classical baselines. A host of key challenges and future directions are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Xuan Tung, Le Tung Giang, Mai Dinh Cong, Pham Dang Anh Duc, Nguyen Hoang Viet, Trinh Van Chien, Lajos Hanzo

item.title: Sequential Change Point Detection for PSK Modulation Switching
item.description: arXiv:2610.14208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transmitters in adaptive communication systems may switch their modulation scheme at an unknown time, and a receiver must detect this switch quickly without raising frequent false alarms. Existing modulation classification methods label a finite block of received data and do not provide stopping rules with controlled false-alarm and delay performance. We study the sequential detection of a switch from one phase shift keying (PSK) scheme to another over an additive white Gaussian noise channel. We build cumulative-sum (CUSUM) and moving-sum (MOSUM) detectors from the log-likelihood ratio and its low-SNR approximation. For a switch from quadrature PSK to binary PSK, we derive the moment-generating function and probability density function of the approximate statistic. We use them to relate the CUSUM threshold to the average run length to false alarm and the worst-case detection delay. For a switch between any two PSK orders, we approximate the vector of overlapping MOSUM statistics as multivariate Gaussian and obtain bounds on both measures. Monte Carlo simulations show that our derived expressions for ARL2FA and WADD closely match the empirical results across thresholds, validating the accuracy of the proposed analytical approximations and theoretical bounds.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Kataria, Davin Sequeira, Arti Yardi

item.title: Orthogonal SC-LDPC Codes for the IDS Channel
item.description: arXiv:2610.14308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a coding scheme for the insertion, deletion and substitution (IDS) channel tailored to the short strands of DNA-based data storage. Instead of an inner synchronisation code, a spatially coupled LDPC (SC-LDPC) code is placed across the strands, with its coupling axis aligned to the position along the strands. Every decoded position thus becomes an anchor to synchronise the neighbouring strands. The decoding waves of the SC-LDPC code carry these anchors from both ends of the strands towards the middle. We bound the achievable rate from above by the information rate of a single strand and from below by that of a separated receiver. For strands of 100 nucleotides (the relevant regime for DNA-based data storage), our scheme outperforms a rate-matched concatenated construction.
item.dc:creator: Frederik Walter, Jessica Bariffi, Antonia Wachter-Zeh

item.title: Low-Latency LDPC Decoding Based on Consensus and Return Residual Belief Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2610.14387v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose two new decoding algorithms for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. The Consensus and Return residual belief propagation (C&R-RBP) algorithm reduces the number of iterations required to achieve a target decoding error rate over an AWGN channel by exploiting the availability of updated information, thereby mitigating the performance degradation caused by the greedy behavior of RBP-based algorithms and reducing error propagation. The Consensus and Delayed Return RBP algorithm (C&DR-RBP) achieves better performance in the early decoding iterations than C&R-RBP, making it particularly suitable for low-latency applications. Both proposed methods maintain the same computational complexity as the original RBP algorithm in terms of residual calculations. We also provide a formal analysis showing that the Consensus mechanism increases the probability of correct bit decisions under initial decoding conditions and in the presence of severe bit transmission errors, providing insight into the performance gains observed in the simulations. Numerical results based on the rapidly growing 5G New Radio (NR) standard, considering different code lengths, code rates, and channel models, demonstrate that both methods outperform competing RBP-based algorithms with similar overall computational complexity in terms of frame error rate (FER) and bit error rate (BER).
item.dc:creator: Allan E. Feitosa, Rodrigo C. de Lamare

item.title: DS and AMDS Symbol-Pair Codes from Three Families of Simple Root Cyclic Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.14435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symbol-pair distances of simple-root cyclic codes are important for evaluating error correction performance under overlapping pair read channels. In this paper, we construct three families of simple-root cyclic codes over finite fields of odd characteristic via generator polynomials. For length \(2q+2\), the minimum symbol-pair distance is \(10\) for every odd prime power \(q\ge 7\), established by excluding invalid support configurations. For length \(4q-4\), when \(q\equiv 3\pmod 4\) and finite field constraints hold, it is \(9\) or \(10\). For length \(2(q-1)\), reciprocal-polynomial analysis shows it is \(11\) or \(12\). All obtained codes are MDS or AMDS symbol-pair codes.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei He, Zihan Zhang, Xiaoqiang Wang, Zhao Lin

item.title: DeepTelecom: A Differentiable Multimodal Framework for Channel Twinning in Dynamic Heterogeneous Wireless Environments
item.description: arXiv:2610.14545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale multimodal data are a key enabler for integrating large generative artificial intelligence models into wireless networks. However, existing wireless datasets offer limited support for heterogeneous environments, particularly in terms of reusable high-fidelity scenes, scalable differentiable ray tracing, and synchronized multimodal data. These limitations are more pronounced in mobile and aerial scenarios with time-varying environments and channels. To address these limitations, we propose DeepTelecom, a material-aware, high-fidelity multimodal channel dataset and reproducible generation framework for networks involving unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. DeepTelecom refines coarse indoor/outdoor reconstructions and uses a large language model to map segmented surfaces to frequency-dependent electromagnetic parameters, yielding material-aware Level of Detail 3 digital twins. Then, a differentiable GPU-accelerated Sionna ray tracer simulates propagation across the sub-6 GHz/millimeter-wave/sub-terahertz bands, and specifically captures rotor-induced micro-Doppler signatures of stationary or moving UAVs at different pitch angles and translational velocities. The framework synchronously produces channel tensors, coverage maps, transmission videos, multi-view images, and weather-conditioned renderings, and supports differentiable material calibration from sparse channel anchors. The released dataset contains 10 material-aware indoor/outdoor scenes and 50,000 synchronized UAV samples; the framework supports scalable generation of additional data for user-defined scenes and system configurations. In 3D UAV localization, DeepTelecom reduces the 90th-percentile error from 31.05 m to 2.43 m compared with schemes considering only channel state information, demonstrating its significance for artificial-intelligence-enabled wireless systems.
item.dc:creator: Bohao Wang, Tianen Yuan, William Yen, Zehua Jiang, Chongwen Huang, Li Wei, Chen Zhu, Jiguang He, Hang Zou, Lina Bariah, Brahim Mefgouda, Anis Bara, Yongliang Shen, Zhaoyang Zhang, Merouane Debbah

item.title: Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.14615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with $k$ bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly $O(2^{k})$ size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.
item.dc:creator: Gal Arnon, Andrej Bogdanov, Paul Lou, Giulio Malavolta, Alon Rosen, Lorenzo Taschin

item.title: Optimal Receive Design on the Observation Axis for RSMA Satellite-UAV Downlinks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A receiver can change its observation state while the physical signal remains the same. In rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) downlinks, this distinction separates receive-beam design and phase-reference transport from the motion of the satellite--UAV line of sight. We formulate receive optimization within the physical--observation dual-axis (PODA) structure and obtain three complementary results. For a known line-of-sight response and positive-definite receiver-noise covariance, a noise-weighted matched combiner simultaneously maximizes every decoding SINR and the minimum user rate. Under directional uncertainty, the principal eigenvector of the conditional response covariance globally maximizes mean array gain; for a Gaussian directional model, an equal-amplitude receiver is optimized by steering towards the conditional mean. Mean rate requires a different objective. We prove that the RSMA common-rate water level is jointly concave in the users' receive gains and derive a semidefinite relaxation with a computable global upper bound. A feasible rank-one beam can therefore be compared directly with the optimum of the finite-scenario problem. We also derive a precision-weighted linear predictor that suppresses uncertain physical-velocity estimates after observation-frame transport. Paired dynamic simulations reduce direction-cosine RMSE by 51.29\% relative to unrestricted nine-point extrapolation. In a separate uncertainty experiment, direct rate optimization increases mean minimum spectral efficiency from 0.32425 to 0.41712 bit/s/Hz, an improvement of 28.64\%; the corresponding design objective is within $2.28\times10^{-4}$ bit/s/Hz of a global upper bound. The phase-transport equation fixes a coherent representative of each optimal beam without changing its gain.
item.dc:creator: Xianwei Meng

item.title: Sum Rate Maximization for Practical RIS-Enhanced Rate-Splitting Multiple Access Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.14765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) combined with rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provide a promising solution for improving the spectral efficiency (SE) of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems. However, most existing studies neglect the practical coupling between the RIS phase shift and amplitude, which may cause phase-shift mismatch and significant performance loss. In this paper, we investigate the multiuser sum-rate maximization problem for practical RIS-enhanced RSMA systems considering amplitude-phase coupling. To address the resulting non-convex problem, an effective variable separation algorithm is proposed. The proposed algorithm is compatible with RIS reflecting optimization under the continuous phase shift or any amplitude-phase coupling relationship and can also be directly extended to practical RIS-enhanced NOMA and OMA systems. Simulation results demonstrate performance gain of over 190\% compared with the ideal-RIS-based benchmark, while the proposed RSMA scheme significantly outperforms the corresponding NOMA and OMA schemes.
item.dc:creator: Qian Zhang, Xuejun Cheng, Jiaming Shi, Yufei Zhao, Rugui Yao, Ye Fan

item.title: MSE Minimization for Movable Antenna Enhanced Wireless Sensing via Array Geometry Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.14882v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops adaptive movable-antenna (MA) array structures to enhance wireless sensing performance under arbitrary SNR conditions, using the AoA estimation MSE as the sensing metric. Due to the presence of strong sidelobes in the ambiguity function of sparse MA arrays, the classical CRB of AoA estimation MSE fails to characterize the true MSE in the low and medium SNR regimes, rendering CRB-optimized antenna position vector designs suboptimal for MA-enabled sensing. We derive a deterministic MSE approximation that captures the local estimation error within the mainlobe of the ambiguity function and the outlier error induced by sidelobes, providing a tractable and accurate optimization objective. We then propose three adaptive MA structures that are tailored to different hardware and computational requirements. For systems with fully independent motors, a movable free array is optimized by a two-stage greedy algorithm, which approaches the performance of the globally optimal exhaustive search but with lower computational complexity. Halving the required motors, a movable nested array fixes the dense inner subarray and adjusts only the outer-subarray spacing, reducing the optimization to a one-dimensional search. As the most hardware-efficient design, a movable twin array is proposed to adjust the inter-subarray spacing only with a single motor, while still achieving significant MSE reduction over fixed array geometries. Numerical results show that the derived approximation closely matches the true MSE compared with existing performance bounds, and that the proposed structures outperform the CRB-optimized designs by orders of magnitude in MSE across the tested low-to-medium SNR range. Moreover, it reveals that in the low-SNR regime, APV reconfiguration is more effective for improving estimation accuracy than simply increasing the number of fixed antennas.
item.dc:creator: Wenrong Chen, Lipeng Zhu, Wenyan Ma, Zhi Chen, Rui Zhang

item.title: Effective DoF Collapse in Sparse Near-Field Beamforming: A Block-Rank-1 Mechanism
item.description: arXiv:2610.15184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse near-field arrays phase-cohere $M$ widely separated sub-arrays of $N$ elements and underpin distributed MIMO, satellite formations, and integrated sensing and communication. We show that their interference suppression over a protected region is set by coherence within a single sub-array rather than by the span of the formation: the effective rank of the region covariance can collapse from $MN$ to $M$. Two independent arguments establish this. For canonical line and disk regions each diagonal covariance block is exactly a classical concentration operator, which supplies sharp per-block rank thresholds and makes fewer than one spatial degree of freedom per sub-array a conservative design rule; an orthogonal decomposition with eigenvalue interlacing gives a nonasymptotic sufficient condition that assumes nothing about the coupling between platforms. The consequences are covariance-side and beamformer-independent: the unloaded Capon functional upper-bounds worst-case signal-to-interference ratio, while its regularized counterpart scales very differently for angularly separated and for in-cone targets. An eight-satellite LEO study validates the theory, including realized worst-case SIR.
item.dc:creator: Changhao He, Xiaojuan Zhang, Francois Chin Po Shin

item.title: Entropy/Length Profile Bounds for the Conversion of (Non)linear Codes in the Merge Regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.15252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Code conversion changes the parameters of encoded data while avoiding complete decoding and re-encoding. Existing general bounds largely rely on the algebraic structure of linear codes. This paper develops an information-theoretic framework for nonlinear code conversion in the merge regime. Using the entropy/length profile (ELP), we derive upper bounds on the number of unchanged symbols and lower bounds on the number of read symbols for arbitrary $(n,M)_q$ codes, without assuming linearity or requiring $\log_q M$ to be an integer. We also obtain joint bounds for multiple initial codes and consequences involving minimum distance. For linear codes, the proposed bounds reduce to the corresponding generalized Hamming weight (GHW) bounds. The construction based on Hamming codes converts Hamming codes of redundancy two into a Hamming code of any larger redundancy and simultaneously attains the general bounds on unchanged and read symbols. The construction based on quasigroups shows that new bounds remain tight for genuinely nonlinear codes of nonintegral dimension and at a nonintegral entropy threshold, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first construction of convertible codes for nonlinear codes.
item.dc:creator: Songping Ge, Han Cai, Xiaohu Tang

item.title: Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receivers for OFDM Systems: An Atomic-Comb Design
item.description: arXiv:2610.15306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg atomic quantum receivers (RAQR) exhibit exceptional sensitivity to radio-frequency (RF) signals, positioning them as promising candidates for next-generation wireless systems. Extending their capabilities to orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), however, requires atomic responses that go beyond broadband reception and are tailored to the structured interference of multicarrier signals. To bridge this gap, we develop an atomic-comb Rydberg receiver based on six-wave mixing (SWM) transduction. In particular, injecting a multi-tone local oscillator (LO) into the RAQR generates frequency-shifted replicas of the intrinsic SWM response. By subtly tuning the amplitude and phase of each LO tone, constructive and destructive interference can be selectively induced to preserve desired response components while attenuating harmful frequency offsets. Furthermore, we harness the response-reshaping capability of the proposed atomic comb to proactively mitigate OFDM interference. More explicitly, by exploiting the discrete difference-frequency structure of both carrier-frequency-offset (CFO)-induced and phase-noise (PN)-induced inter-carrier interference (ICI), we optimize the atomic-comb response to suppress dominant ICI components directly. We further reveal an intrinsic coupling between spectral shaping and the time-domain effective channel memory, motivating a joint optimization of both ICI and inter-symbol interference (ISI), which simultaneously suppresses inter-carrier leakage and post-cyclic-prefix (CP) tail energy. Extensive simulation results validate our atomic-comb design, unveiling that the proposed atomic comb can effectively reshape the receiver response over the OFDM, while mitigating ICI, shortening the effective channel memory, and substantially lowering CP overhead.
item.dc:creator: Yuanbin Chen, Chong Meng Samson See, Chau Yuen

item.title: New Minimum Storage Regenerating Codes With Small Sub-packetization Levels for All Admissible Repair Degrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.15329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, {we propose a new family of $(n, k)$ Minimum Storage Regenerating (MSR) codes} for distributed storage systems. By structuring the parity-check matrix as a block Vandermonde matrix composed of diagonal matrices and generalized permutation matrices, the proposed code achieves a sub-packetization level of $N = (d-k+1)^{\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil}$ and supports any repair degree $k+1\le d<n$. A key innovation of the new construction lies in relaxing the strict commutativity condition previously required for the building blocks in the parity-check matrices of Ye-Barg codes. We introduce a novel proof technique to establish the MDS property without relying on full commutativity, thereby generalizing the applicability of block Vandermonde matrices and enriching the family of Ye-Barg codes. Additionally, the sparsity of the parity-check matrix enhances encoding and decoding efficiency by reducing computational complexity. This work provides new insights into the construction of MSR codes.
item.dc:creator: Jie Li, Xiaohu Tang, Linqi Song

item.title: Wyner's Common Information and the Common Entropy are NP-Hard to Compute
item.description: arXiv:2610.15402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wyner's common information $J(p)$ and the common entropy $G(p)$ of a pair of random variables $(X,Y)$ with finite ranges and joint distribution $p$ are both defined by an optimization over the auxiliary random variables $W$ that make $X$ and $Y$ conditionally independent: $J(p)$ is the infimum of the mutual information $I(X,Y;W)$, and $G(p)$ is the infimum of the entropy $H(W)$. We prove that both quantities are NP-hard to compute. For Wyner's common information, deciding whether $J(p)$ is strictly smaller than a given integer $r$ is NP-hard, and the problem is NP-complete on tables that are uniform on their support and have the same number of positive entries in every row. The reduction is from Maximum Edge Biclique and rests on an exact criterion, in terms of rectangles in the support of $p$, for improving on the auxiliary $W=X$; every yes-instance satisfies $J(p)<r-1/(4N^2)$ and every no-instance satisfies $J(p)=r$, where $N$ is the number of positive entries of $p$. For the common entropy, deciding whether $G(p)\le r$ for a rational number $r$ is NP-hard, even for tables with at most four nonzero entries in each row, all taking one of two values. The reduction is from exact cover by $3$-sets and rests on a majorization property of the masses of the nonnegative rank-one decompositions of $p$, combined with a quantitative form of the Schur concavity of entropy. In both cases the separation between yes- and no-instances is inverse-polynomial in the size of $p$, so that approximating $J(p)$ or $G(p)$ within a suitable inverse-polynomial additive error is also NP-hard. The two mechanisms are genuinely different: we exhibit a table on which a large rectangle in the support lowers $J$ below the threshold of our first reduction while leaving $G$ on it.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Bruno, Ugo Vaccaro

item.title: Insdel Reed-Solomon Decoding Algorithms up to the Half-Singleton Bound
item.description: arXiv:2610.15413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we focus on decoding optimal Reed-Solomon codes of dimension two for insdel errors up to the half-Singleton bound. We present a decoding algorithm for the general insertion-and-deletion scenario with a time complexity smaller than brute-force decoding. Our algorithm corrects insdel errors up to the half-Singleton bound, which exceeds the scope of existing methods. Additionally, for the special cases of insertion-only and deletion-only insdel error patterns, we present two different algorithms with a time complexity smaller than our general algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Bencheng Fan, Margreta Kuijper, Jingge Zhu

item.title: An Upper Bound to the Undetected Error Exponent with Erasure Decoding at Positive Rates
item.description: arXiv:2610.15420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the undetected-error exponent of discrete memoryless channels with erasure decoding. Assuming that the undetected-error and erasure probabilities vanish, we derive an upper bound on the undetected-error exponent at positive rates. The bound uses Somekh-Baruch's genie-aided argument where an auxiliary output provides the decoder with a list of codewords. It recovers Telatar's tight rate-zero converse and is at least as tight as the straight-line bound. A numerical example shows that the improvement over the straight-line bound can be strict.
item.dc:creator: Seyed AmirPouya Moeini, Marco Dalai, Albert Guill\'en i F\`abregas

item.title: Universal Decoding for Unequal Error Protection
item.description: arXiv:2610.15423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study universal unequal error protection of a single special message over discrete memoryless channels. We construct a sequence of codes with a decoding rule that does not depend on the channel transition law. We derive an achievable error exponent for the special message while ensuring reliable decoding of the ordinary messages. The resulting exponent strictly improves on the natural equal-error-protection random-coding baseline and remains positive as the rate approaches capacity. For symmetric channels, it converges to the optimal red-alert exponent at capacity.
item.dc:creator: Seyed AmirPouya Moeini, Albert Guill\'en i F\`abregas

item.title: SiteEvo: An LLM Agent for Autonomous Discovery of Site-Adaptive Massive MIMO Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.15490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing a massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) detector that is tailored to each specific deployment site can improve detection performance, yet most existing detectors, including deep-unfolding methods, adapt mainly within human-prescribed algorithmic structures. This letter proposes SiteEvo, a site-adaptive agentic discovery framework that extends adaptation from parameter tuning to detector-algorithm discovery. Rather than selecting or recombining predefined architectures, the large language model (LLM) agent synthesizes complete executable detector programs under a common design contract by combining its pretrained communication knowledge, site-specific wireless evidence, and experience accumulated during the search. Each proposal defines its own processing structure and trainable parameterization, and the parameters are optimized by a communication-system backend. The resulting high-performance detector is further structurally refined to reduce block-level computational cost under a bit error rate (BER)-preservation constraint and is finally frozen for deployment without online LLM inference. Simulations across three sites demonstrate BER reductions by factors of 2.6 to 6.0 over the best-performing competing detector at each site at 6 dB, while structural refinement reduces block-level computational cost by 16.7-34.1% under a validation-BER constraint.
item.dc:creator: Jiajia Guo, Chao-Kai Wen, Shi Jin, Jun Zhang

item.title: Rate-Distortion Theory of Gaussian Mixtures via Posterior Label Sampling
item.description: arXiv:2610.15549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the mean-squared error (MSE) rate-distortion function (RDF) of finite Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in $\mathbb{R}^d$, for which neither the RDF nor an optimal test channel is known in closed form. It can be sandwiched between the genie-aided conditional RDF $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)$, which can be characterized in closed-form for a GMM, and $R_{\mathbf{X} | T}(D)+I(\mathbf{X};T)$, where $T$ denotes the latent component label. We show that the upper bound can be achieved operationally by the proposed Gibbs-relabelling method (GRM), which conveys a label from the posterior $P_{T|\mathbf{X}}$ through \textit{channel simulation} at rate $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, followed by vector quantization of the resulting exactly Gaussian conditional sources by reverse water-filling. Using the Shannon lower bound (SLB), we prove that GRM attains the SLB, and hence the RDF, of a general finite mixture if and only if every component attains its own SLB. For a GMM this holds throughout the fully active interval $D/d<\min_{k,m}\lambda_{k,m}$, where $\lambda_{k,m}$ are the eigenvalues of the component covariances, and for scalar GMMs the condition is also necessary. Since GRM cannot operate below the label cost $I(\mathbf{X};T)$, we propose a complementary stochastic scalar quantization (SSQ) scheme for low rates, which simulates an $M$-ary reconstruction index. We show that at low rates SSQ with $M\geq 2$ matches the Shannon RDF to first order: $R(D_{\max}-\delta)=\delta/(2\tau^2)+o(\delta)$, where $\tau^2$ is a directional sub-Gaussian proxy of the mixture, and quantify the price of a finite codebook through a strict rate gap at high rates and a distortion floor whose joint scaling in $M$ and number of mixture components is characterized. Numerical results illustrate both regimes and the finite-blocklength cost of channel simulation.
item.dc:creator: Weichen Wang, Deniz G\"und\"uz

item.title: Binary Codes Correcting Multiple Edits via Polynomial Hashing and Entropy Recycling
item.description: arXiv:2610.15631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Codes in the Levenshtein metric that can correct multiple edits (including deletions, insertions, and substitutions) have attracted a lot of attention recently owing to their application in DNA-based storage and racetrack memories. In this work, we present new techniques for designing explicit binary codes of length $n$ that correct $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. We first propose to use a polynomial hash to construct a systematic code that corrects $t$ edits with $(4t+2)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Then we observe that there are many polynomial hashes like this, some are good, some are bad. So, we propose the second technique, called entropy recycling, to use the indices of good hashes to carry information. As a consequence, we obtain a partial-systematic code of length $n$ that corrects $t$ edits with at most $(2t+1)\log n+O_t(\log\log n)$ bits of redundancy. Finally, we provide deterministic polynomial-time encoding and decoding algorithms for our code.
item.dc:creator: Quan D. Bui, Shuche Wang, Van Khu Vu

item.title: Exact Sampling Under Campbell Cost via R\'enyi Channel Simulation Divergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.15656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the communication cost of exact sampling under Campbell's exponential coding criterion. Given a target distribution $P$ and a proposal distribution $Q$, the sender and receiver share i.i.d. $Q$-distributed samples, and the sender communicates an index so that the selected sample has distribution exactly $P$. We introduce a new information measure R\'enyi channel simulation divergence $R_\alpha(P\Vert Q)$, a R\'enyi generalization of the channel simulation divergence. We then show that it lower bounds the Campbell cost of every exact sampler and is achievable, via a new layered sampling scheme, within an additive constant depending only on the Campbell parameter. This yields a tighter one-shot characterization than previous bounds based on R\'enyi divergences of different orders. For i.i.d. product distributions, under suitable non-degeneracy and moment conditions, we further show that the gap beyond the leading R\'enyi-divergence term is $\frac{1}{2}\log n+O(1)$.
item.dc:creator: Yijun Fan, Aaron B. Wagner

item.title: Correcting Burst Errors with Applications to DNA-Based Data Storage
item.description: arXiv:2610.15701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the problem of permutation burst error-correction, motivated by applications in molecular data storage with nanopore sequencing read platforms. A permutation burst of length $k$ is an error that affects a substring of length $k$ of a string of length $n$ by permuting its entries. Permutation burst errors can be corrected using classical burst error-correcting codes, such as Fire and Reed-Solomon codes. Here, we study how to reduce the redundancy of these classical codes by taking into account that the burst error preserves the weight of the substring. In addition, we further restrict our model to handle cyclic permutation bursts only, which are of independent practical and mathematical interest. Our main results include proving/establishing the following: a) for $k=o(\sqrt{n}),$ the redundancy of any permutation burst error correcting code is at least $\log n-k+\log \binom{2k-2}{k-2}+o(1).$ This result follows from McDiarmid's concentration bound; b) for $k \geq 9$ and $k=o\left(\sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}}\right)$, the redundancy of any cyclic permutation burst error correcting code is at least $\log n +\log (k(k-1)-56)-\log\,80+o(1).$ c) the asymptotic redundancy upper bounds for the two types of substring errors that are twice the lower bound; d) constructions for both permutation burst and cyclic permutation burst errors that involve Varshamov-Tenegoltz type constraints or represent generalizations and extensions of Fire and other codes. In particular, we exhibit polynomially encodable and decodable codes that can correct cyclic bursts of length $\leq k$ using $\log n + k + 49\log k + O(\log \log k)$ redundant bits.
item.dc:creator: Yuan-Pon Chen, Olgica Milenkovic

item.title: On the Average List Size of VT Codes under Two Insertions or Two Deletions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Levenshtein's classical theorem shows that any code that can uniquely decode from \(t\) deletions can also uniquely decode from \(t\) insertions. This symmetry, however, does not generally hold in the list-decoding regime. Several prior results on the capacity and radii of list-decoding from insertions and deletions suggest that insertions are easier to handle than deletions. In an effort to better understand this asymmetry between insertions and deletions under list-decoding, we study an analogous version of McEliece's \emph{average list size problem}. More precisely, given a binary code \(\mathcal{C}\) of length \(n\) that uniquely corrects \(t'\) insertions (or deletions), we are interested in the average number of codewords returned by a \(t\)-insertion (or deletion) list decoder, where \(t' < t\). Focusing on the case of \(t'=1\) and \(t=2\), we find that under two insertions, this quantity is at most \((n+12)/4\) for any VT code of length \(n\), whereas under two deletions it is at least \(n/2 - 10\) when averaged over all length-\(n\) VT codes. The nearly factor-of-two gap between these upper and lower bounds serves to confirm the relative ease of list-decoding of insertions compared to deletions from an average-case perspective.
item.dc:creator: Anisha Banerjee, Roni Con, Antonia Wachter-Zeh, Eitan Yaakobi

item.title: Superpolynomial Lists for Reed-Solomon Codes over Binary Extension Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.15815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work shows that ordinary Reed--Solomon codes over prime fields admit polynomial-size lists up to list-decoding capacity on every evaluation set. We show a contrasting phenomenon over binary extension fields. For every fixed rate $0<R<1$, there exists $\varepsilon_R>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $h$, the full-field Reed--Solomon code over $\mathbb{F}_{2^h}$ has a received word with $n^{\Omega_R(\log n)}$ codewords within relative distance $1-R-\varepsilon_R$. To our knowledge, these are the first superpolynomial ordinary Reed--Solomon list-size lower bounds at fixed positive rate and a fixed positive agreement gap above the rate. Thus capacity-approaching polynomial list size for Reed--Solomon codes is not uniform over the underlying field, and the obstruction occurs at every fixed rate. As a puncturing consequence, the same holds for primitive Reed--Solomon codes; the obstruction is also robust under controlled dense puncturing. The proof begins with an exact correspondence that turns certain binary Bose--Chaudhuri--Hocquenghem weight-enumerator coefficients into sizes of single Reed--Solomon lists. A classical binary weight family gives the initial quarter-rate construction, while a quadratic-form enumeration supplies its superpolynomial multiplicity. A common-kernel quotient/descent argument and common-root padding then extend the construction to all rates. We also determine the optimized agreement envelope achieved by the construction.
item.dc:creator: Minshen Zhu

item.title: Residual-Information Generalization Bounds Under Selective Privacy: Extended Version
item.description: arXiv:2610.15847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Information-theoretic generalization bounds usually control dependence on the task sample, whereas selective privacy may constrain only a different, private coordinate. We study i.i.d. pairs $(X,Y)$, where a learner observes $(X^n,Y^n)$, leaks at most $\epsilon_n$ nats about $X^n$, and incurs loss on $Y$. A chain-rule transfer converts this mismatched constraint into the closed-form universal certificate $I(W;Y^n)\leq\min\{nH(Y),nH(Y\mid X)+\epsilon_n\}$. Combining the certificate with mutual-information generalization yields a bound governed by residual task uncertainty and normalized privacy leakage. We derive complementary task-compression and individual-sample refinements, identify a sharp obstruction showing why selective privacy alone need not give a vanishing certificate, and invert the bound to obtain the exact leakage allowance for a prescribed generalization tolerance. We prove exact information-level achievability for deterministic-task and independent-residual source families and show that the resulting $\sqrt{\epsilon_n/n}$ generalization rate is tight up to a universal constant. We also give a fixed-horizon adaptive application in which conditional leakage costs add.
item.dc:creator: Amirreza Zamani, Parastoo Sadeghi, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: Low-Latency Belief-Propagation Decoding of Quantum LDPC Codes with Reinforcement-Learned Scheduling
item.description: arXiv:2610.15857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Belief propagation (BP) is attractive for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) decoding because of its low complexity and low latency, but short cycles and degeneracy can limit its error-correction performance. Reinforcement-learned sequential scheduling (RL-S) substantially improves this performance by adapting the variable node (VN) update order, although Q-table storage and heap-based selection introduce additional overhead. We propose bucket RL-S (B-RL-S), which quantizes learned Q-values into integer priorities and schedules VN updates using dynamically maintained first-in, first-out buckets. Without retraining or changing the BP message updates, B-RL-S reduces policy storage and refreshes only priorities affected by local residual syndrome changes. A fixed number of priority levels enables constant-time VN selection and queue relocation. For the $[[288,12,18]]$ bivariate bicycle code over the depolarizing channel at $p=0.05$, B-RL-S with eight priority levels achieves approximately one fifth the block error rate (BLER) of flooding BP followed by order-10 ordered-statistics decoding. The respective caps are $1000$ sequential iterations for B-RL-S and $1000$ flooding iterations for the BP stage of the reference decoder. These results highlight strong error correction with inexpensive scheduling and no additional post-processing stage.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Moradi, Ghilas Aissou, Taejoon Kim, Remi A. Chou, David G. M. Mitchell

item.title: Higher-order nonhomomorphicity under affine restrictions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the behavior of the $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity of Boolean functions under restriction to affine subspaces. For odd $k\ge3$ and $0\le t<n$, we introduce the $t$-restriction $k$-th-order nonhomomorphicity $P_{k,t}(f)$, defined as the minimum of $P_k(f_{\mid A})$ over affine spaces of codimension at most $t$. For a direct sum of $m$ monomials of degrees at least two, we determine $P_{k,t}$ exactly. When $t<m$, a minimum is obtained by setting one variable equal to zero in each of the $t$ monomials of lowest degree. When $m\le t<n$, the minimum is zero. The proof combines multiplicativity of even Walsh moments with a contraction argument for affine restrictions. We establish a general formula for the Walsh transform of a Boolean function restricted to an affine subspace of arbitrary codimension, yielding an exact spectral characterization of the $t$-restriction normalized nonlinearity $\rnnl_t(f)$. As odd $k$ tends to infinity, $(1-2P_{k,t}(f))^{1/(k+1)}$ converges to $1-2\rnnl_t(f)$. We further prove that every non-affine function has a hyperplane restriction with strictly smaller odd-order nonhomomorphicity. Finally, we determine $\rnnl_1(T_{d,n})$ exactly for all threshold functions with $n\ge3$. This proves the two threshold-function conjectures left open in~\cite{SergeAnaPante2025}, including the previously unresolved odd-majority case, where a minimizing hyperplane is $x_1+x_2=0$.
item.dc:creator: Serge Feukoua, Ana S\u{a}l\u{a}gean, Pantelimon St\u{a}nic\u{a}

item.title: Fine asymptotics for approximate simulation of symmetric channels
item.description: arXiv:2610.15877v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximate channel simulation problem in the normal approximation regime. Our starting point is the fact established by Cao et al.~\cite{Cao_channel_simulation}, that the minimal codebook size $M_\epsilon^*(W)$ for a fixed error tolerance $\epsilon>0$ is closely related to the $\epsilon$-smooth channel max-information, $I_{\max}^\epsilon(W)$. Using this, we refine earlier large-blocklength approximations to $M_\epsilon^*(W^{\otimes n})$ for discrete memoryless channels. Specifically, we provide tight third-order expansions for Gallager-symmetric channels and demonstrate that the third-order term is channel-dependent. As in corresponding channel coding expansions, we identify a substantial rate gap between singular and nonsingular channels. Notably, the direction of this gap is reversed relative to channel coding: The third-order term is $-\frac{1}{2}\log n$ for singular channels but $O(\log\log n)$ for nonsingular channels.
item.dc:creator: Valentinian Lungu, Aaron B. Wagner, Ioannis Kontoyiannis

item.title: Exact Privacy--Distortion Design of Support-Constrained Randomized Response
item.description: arXiv:2610.15972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-support local randomizers can incur unnecessary reporting distortion on ordered alphabets. We study randomized response whose output is restricted to a radius-$t$ neighborhood of the private input. Input-dependent supports create privacy leakage at their boundaries, so ordinary likelihood-ratio calibration is no longer sufficient. Under approximate local privacy restricted to input pairs at distance at most $H$, we derive the exact hockey-stick defect of the mechanism. We then solve the joint design of the truthful probability, off-truth probability, and support radius. The fixed-radius optimum is available in closed form, while the global optimum requires only a one-dimensional integer search. We characterize both the privacy floor and its inverse, namely the smallest defect attainable under a reporting-distortion budget. We further prove that stringent approximate privacy forces the support size to scale as $\Omega(H/\delta)$. Deterministic evaluations illustrate the resulting tradeoff.
item.dc:creator: Amirreza Zamani, Parastoo Sadeghi, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: Embedding Information in Policy Randomness: Distribution-Preserving Implicit Communication in MDPs
item.description: arXiv:2610.15976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a new role of randomness in stochastic policies--as a medium for embedding and communicating information. Specifically, we consider an agent interacting with an environment according to a prescribed stochastic policy. By carefully modulating the random action realizations of the policy, information can be embedded into the agent's behavior without altering the prescribed action distribution. We cast this problem as a channel coding problem, in which the controlled system implicitly serves as a communication channel. We then propose a coding scheme, termed posterior-matching randomness modulation (PRAM), that selects actions according to the message to be transmitted. With the aid of common randomness independent of the control system, PRAM preserves the prescribed action distribution for every state and every message. We further prove that PRAM is asymptotically reliable: the message can be decoded with arbitrarily small error probability as the observed state trajectory becomes sufficiently long. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in applications including multi-bit policy watermarking and trajectory provenance.
item.dc:creator: Gongpu Chen, Deniz G\"und\"uz

item.title: Delay-Doppler Duality: Simplifying Exact Equalization of Zak-OTFS in Time or in Frequency
item.description: arXiv:2610.16033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Zak-OTFS carrier waveform is a pulse in the delay-Doppler (DD) domain, and given the input-output (I/O) relation at one DD point in a frame, we can predict the I/O relation at all other points. While it is simple to acquire the effective wireless channel with Zak-OTFS, the cost of embracing inter-carrier interference is equalization complexity. The cost of linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) equalization grows cubically with the frame size. We describe how to use channel knowledge to reduce equalization complexity. For any pulse shaping filter, and for fractional delays and Dopplers, we show that the DD channel matrix is unitarily similar, through the discrete Zak transform, to a time-domain (TD) matrix that is a weighted sum of cyclic delay and Doppler operators, where the weights are the taps of the effective channel. We also obtain a dual frequency-domain (FD) form through an additional Fourier transform. The TD matrix is banded with a width set by the delay spread that is independent of the Doppler spread, whereas the FD matrix is banded with a width set only by the Doppler spread. We design a receiver that reads off the two widths from the channel estimate, selects the cheaper domain, and solves the banded system exactly, using a bordered Cholesky factorization that treats the quasi-periodic wrap-around without sacrificing degrees of freedom. Filters that decay slowly need a few preconditioned conjugate gradient steps. We show that the complexity of equalization becomes linear in the frame size. Simulations match direct DD-LMMSE error rates with three to four orders of magnitude fewer multiplications. A single receiver handles channels with very different delay and Doppler characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Mudasir Ahmad Sheikh, Robert Calderbank

item.title: Robust Quickest Change Detection with Cost-Efficient Experiment Design and Unknown Post-Change Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A quickest change detection problem is studied where the decision-maker has access to multiple experiments, but can choose only one experiment at a time to detect the change. The true post-change distribution under each experiment is unknown, but known to belong to a family of distributions. It is assumed that each of these families of distributions has an element that is least favorable in a well-defined sense. An algorithm is proposed that is designed using the least favorable distributions. It is shown that the algorithm is first-order asymptotically optimal, as the rate of false alarms goes to zero. This algorithm minimizes the worst-case average detection delay over all post-change distributions within the assumed families, subject to a constraint on the average run length to false alarm and constraints on the average fraction of time each experiment is performed before change.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Vincent Lubenia, Taposh Banerjee

item.title: Fourier entropy of threshold functions and their compositions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the Fourier entropy--influence inequality for every linear threshold function, with a constant below $8.937$ and no restrictions on its weights or threshold. The argument applies to regular Boolean functions and gives logarithmic bounds for their Boolean combinations and for unions with bounded variable overlap. Character multiplication preserves the estimates and yields bounds by influence minus variance. Under arbitrary product measures, symmetric thresholds satisfy the strengthened inequality needed for read-once composition, uniformly in depth and fan-in. A joint description of each Fourier set refines the overlap estimate and recovers constant bounds for addressing. Exact selector identities extend the bound to orthogonal multiplexers with shared data. Rare activation preserves the optimal constant of unrestricted FEI. The proofs combine pivotal antichains, spectral reference measures, and product-measure composition.
item.dc:creator: Yitzchak Shmalo

item.title: Double circulant LCD codes over $\mathbb{F}_2+u\mathbb{F}_2$ and constructions for binary LCD codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear complementary dual (LCD) codes are linear codes that intersect their dual trivially. We study double circulant (Euclidean) LCD codes over the finite chain ring $R=\mathbb F_2+u\mathbb F_2$, where $u^2=0$. Using the Chinese Remainder Theorem and the factorization of $x^n-1$, we derive an explicit enumeration formula, with a separate treatment of the constituent corresponding to $x-1$, which is not obtained by a formal specialization of the previously known counting formula over $\mathbb F_q[u]/(u^k)$. Assuming Artin's primitive root conjecture for $2$, we show that the binary Gray images contain an asymptotically good family of rate $1/2$ whose relative distance can approach $H_2^{-1}(1/4)$ from below. More importantly from the constructive viewpoint, by combining Gray images with a known extension construction, we obtain a binary LCD code with parameters $[29,15,7]$ and construct two explicit permutation-inequivalent binary LCD codes with parameters $[45,23,9]$.
item.dc:creator: Xingxing Xu, Minjia Shi, Jon-Lark Kim

item.title: Learning Rules, Memorizing Facts: An Information-Theoretic View of Hallucination
item.description: arXiv:2610.16233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the relationship between generalization and hallucination requires clarifying the role of memorization. We study this relationship from an information-theoretic perspective through a Selector-Density Conditional Mutual Information (CMI) framework. In the sparse random-fact limit, a uniformly bounded information budget per fact forces a nonvanishing false-positive rate at recall bounded away from zero, even when all facts are observed during training. In a rules-and-facts setting, we decompose model-data mutual information into rule learning, atomic-fact memory, and excess memorization, revealing competition between rule learning and factual memory even without excess memorization. A joint budget bound quantifies the resulting constraint on atomic hallucination under perfect atomic recall. Moreover, an additive Gaussian model shows that maintaining high recall for atomic and composite facts incurs false positives even under optimal data mixing. Finally, controlled relational experiments hint how training exposure, rule complexity, and model capacity shape these trade-offs.
item.dc:creator: Gengze Xu, Anxin Guo, Yifei Hu, Xiangyu Wu, Yong Liu, Ziqiao Wang

item.title: RPA Decoding with Few Subspace Projections for Correcting Structured Error Patterns in RM Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Recursive Projection Aggregation (RPA) decoder for Reed-Muller codes uses, in its default implementation, all one-dimensional subspaces at each level of recursion. We restrict our attention to the case where the number of errors is $t<d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$. It is known that if the number of errors is $t<d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$, then $2t+1$ subspaces at each level of recursion are sufficient to correct these errors. We show that, for structured error patterns, the number of subspaces required for correction can be reduced further by appropriately selecting the subspaces used for projection. In particular, when errors occur as a single burst of length $t < d_{\mathrm{min}}/2$, three subspaces at each level of recursion suffice for correction. We obtain similar results for multiple bursts and other structured error patterns as well.
item.dc:creator: Shiv Pratap Singh Rathore, Navin Kashyap

item.title: Generalized Hamming Weights and Subcode Support Weight Distributions of Twisted Reed-Solomon Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we determine the generalized Hamming weight hierarchies of two classes of twisted Reed--Solomon (TRS) codes. For TRS codes with one twist, we first determine all possible values of the generalized Hamming weights. We then give a complete characterization of the weight hierarchy in terms of the minimum distance of the dual code. Explicit conditions are derived for the minimum distances of the code and its dual, which make the whole weight hierarchy explicitly computable. As special cases, the obtained results recover several known characterizations for TRS codes to be MDS, NMDS codes, and $s$-gap AMDS codes. For TRS codes with two twists, we similarly determine the complete generalized Hamming weight hierarchy. In this case, the higher generalized Hamming weights are determined by the first two generalized Hamming weights of the dual code, for which explicit rank conditions are also obtained. In addition, we further determine the subcode support weight distributions of this class of single-twist TRS codes. More precisely, for each $1 \le r \le k$, we derive an explicit formula for the number of $r$-dimensional subcodes with a prescribed support size, thereby giving a complete description of the support distribution of subcodes.
item.dc:creator: Chao Liu, Hao Chen, Dabin Zheng, Yaqi Chen

item.title: More Interactions Make Communications More Efficient: A Directed Information Bottleneck Approach to Task-Oriented Communication
item.description: arXiv:2610.16328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task-oriented communication improves communication efficiency by transmitting semantic information required for downstream tasks, but may incur redundancy with previously transmitted information. To address this issue, we propose a variational directed information bottleneck joint source-channel coding (VDIB-JSCC) framework that transmits only previously unacquired information. Specifically, we use directed information to characterize the causal flow of task-relevant incremental information and theoretically demonstrate its advantages over mutual information and conditional mutual information. Based on this metric, we formulate a directed information bottleneck (DIB) objective that balances task-relevant information preservation and redundant information compression. We further derive a variational formulation, termed VDIB, whose tractable upper bound serves as the training loss. The encoder integrates a Vision Transformer for frame-wise semantic extraction and a Mamba-based causal state-space model for capturing temporal dependencies and extracting incremental information, while the decoder uses a Mamba-based state-space model for task inference. Experiments on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 video streams demonstrate that VDIB-JSCC achieves higher classification accuracy with less transmitted information than state-of-the-art semantic communication methods. These results show that leveraging historical knowledge enables task completion with less information, improving communication efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Zhirun Zheng, Yiqin Deng, Phone Lin, Yuguang Fang

item.title: Log Density Spectrum Based Decoding of Polar Codes for Channels with Strong Phase Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.16363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A decoding method is proposed for polar codes under channels with strong phase noise. In contrast to traditional SC decoding, where recursions are performed on scalar soft information such as probabilities, the proposed decoding recurses over probability density functions defined on the phase-noise variable. To make the density-level recursion computationally tractable, we represent each log-density by its spectrum, and derive approximate formulas for the spectrum recursion, therefore, the proposed method is termed log-density spectrum recursion (LDSR). Numerical results are given under strong phase noise and AWGN, showing that a prominent superiority of error performance is achieved by LDSR in comparison with traditional SC and Kalman-based methods.
item.dc:creator: Yinuo Mei, Daiming Qu

item.title: Multiple-Function Approximated Coded Computing: Constructions and Error Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.16549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coded computing mitigates stragglers in distributed computation. While Lagrange coded computing (LCC) enables exact polynomial computation over finite fields, Berrut approximated coded computing (BACC) enables approximate computation of arbitrary, including non-polynomial, functions in the analog domain. In applications such as multi-task learning and inference, multiple functions must be evaluated over different subsets of a common dataset, making single-round computation desirable to reduce communication overhead. An existing LCC approach addresses this requirement but is restricted to polynomial functions over finite fields, leaving single-round multi-function computation in the analog domain an open problem. In this work, we develop a single-round construction for computing multiple arbitrary functions using BACC. We first extend the existing multi-function computation approach in LCC to the BACC setting and derive an approximation-error bound. Building on this, we propose a construction based on Berrut basis functions for computing multiple arbitrary functions and derive its approximation-error bound. We analyze the scaling of both bounds with the number of functions and the number of data points per function, and numerically compare the two constructions over a wide range of arbitrary functions. The results demonstrate that the proposed construction achieves lower relative errors than the existing approach in the tested settings.
item.dc:creator: Rimpi Borah, Wilton Kim, J. Harshan, Stanislav Kruglik, Han Mao Kiah

item.title: Covering Radius and Deep Holes of Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon Codes under the NRT Metric
item.description: arXiv:2610.16643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deep hole problem is a fundamental problem in coding theory, and it has many important applications in code constructions and cryptography. The deep hole problem of Reed-Solomon codes has gained a lot of attention. As a generalization of Reed-Solomon codes under Hamming metric, we study the covering radius and deep holes of Hyperderivative Reed-Solomon (HRS) codes under the Niederreiter-Rosenbloom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric. We determine the NRT covering radius of HRS code and characterize its NRT deep holes via Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) extensions and polynomial remainder conditions. We further relate the enumeration of NRT deep holes to the characteristic polynomial of an associated hyperplane arrangement. We also provide three classes of explicit NRT deep-hole constructions, propose a Cheng-Murray type conjecture for HRS codes under the NRT metric and obtain a conditional low-layer description. Using these characterizations, we derive exact enumeration formulas in several special cases.
item.dc:creator: Zhihao Zhu, Haojie Gu, Jun Zhang, Yu Li

item.title: On Measures of Dissimilarity on the Majorization Simplex
item.description: arXiv:2610.16687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The majorization simplex $\mathcal{P}_n$ is the set of probability vectors of length $n$ whose entries are arranged in non-increasing order. Under the majorization order, $\mathcal{P}_n$ is a lattice, and it is the natural space for comparing distributions when the labels of the outcomes are not relevant. In this work, we study measures of dissimilarity (and, similarity) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. Our first set of results concerns the R\'enyi-entropy based distance $d_\alpha(p,q)=H_\alpha(p)+H_\alpha(q)-2H_\alpha(p\vee q)$ proposed by Yadav and Shkel (2026), which generalizes a metric of Cicalese, Gargano and Vaccaro (2013). We show that $d_\alpha$ is a metric on $\mathcal{P}_n$ for $\alpha\in[1,\infty)$, while for $\alpha\in[0,1)\cup\{\infty\}$, $d_\alpha$ is not a metric in general. Our main result in this part identifies the necessary and sufficient conditions for equality in the triangle inequality of $d_\alpha$ when $\alpha>1$, for which we identify the equality conditions for the supermodularity of the R\'enyi entropy $H_\alpha$. Our second set of results concerns the total variation distance and the Hellinger affinity (also called the Bhattacharyya coefficient) on $\mathcal{P}_n$. We obtain a number of bounds on these measures, along with some of their equality conditions. The resulting Hellinger affinity based upper bound on the total variation distance can be smaller than the bounds obtained from Pinsker's and the Bretagnolle--Huber inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Tarun Hariharan, Prasad Krishnan, Abhishek Deshpande

item.title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
item.description: arXiv:2610.16707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Xinjie, Dier Tang, Shaolun-Huang

item.title: Digital-Twin-Referenced Belief-Guided Q-Learning for Jammer Identification and Beam-Power Control in a mmWave Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digital Twin (DT) combined with reinforcement learning (RL) can support adaptive resource allocation and security-aware decision-making by comparing expected and observed network behavior. This paper presents a simulation-based DT reference and a belief-guided Q-learning (BGQL) for joint jammer identification and beam-power control in a site-specific 28-GHz network. For each action, the same channel simulator is evaluated under an attack-free and an attacked configuration. Receiver-level residuals are combined with spatial jamming footprints and accumulated to form a normalized suspicion vector. BGQL incorporates this vector into an aggregated state, a belief-concentration reward, and exploratory beam-selection rule. The BGQL scheme is compared with SARSA, Greedy, and Random under matched attacker sets. Across 30 paired Monte Carlo runs in four configurations, with the number of active jammers supplied to every method, BGQL achieves mean aggregate full-band link-rate scores of approximately 437.4--564.2~Mbit/s and rate-to-device-power scores of 60.37--76.79~Mbit/J. Its detection accuracy is 100\% in one-jammer configurations and approximately 78\%--81\% in two-jammer configurations. BGQL requires approximately 80--130~s per run, compared with 5--14~s for SARSA, reflecting evaluation of 625 beam pairs during exploratory steps. These findings provide a matched-model simulation proof of concept for DT-referenced belief-guided learning for security-aware beam-power control in 6G networks.
item.dc:creator: Parmida Geranmayeh, Onur G\"unl\"u

item.title: Information-Theoretic Limits for Rectangular Spiked Matrix Models with Rotationally Invariant Noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.16797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the information-theoretic limits of inference in rectangular rank-one spiked matrix models with additive rotationally invariant noise, thereby going beyond the standard assumption of independent noise entries. Using the replica method from statistical physics, we derive a variational formula for the mutual information between the signal and the data, together with a system of saddle point equations predicting the minimum mean squared error in estimating the rank-one spike. We further show that, in the Bayes-optimal setting, these saddle point equations coincide with the fixed point equations of the state evolution of a recently proposed orthogonal approximate message passing algorithm with Bayes-optimal denoisers. This equivalence provides an algorithmic interpretation of the replica prediction and supports the Bayes-optimality of orthogonal approximate message passing whenever the relevant fixed point is unique. Numerical evaluations of the saddle point equations for several rotationally invariant noise ensembles and signal priors, together with finite-size simulations of the algorithm, confirm the asymptotic predictions. They illustrate both regimes with a unique informative fixed point, where orthogonal approximate message passing is predicted to attain the minimum mean squared error, and regimes with multiple fixed points, where a statistical-to-computational gap exists.
item.dc:creator: Qun Chen, Rudy Skerk, Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Junjie Ma, Haochuan Zhang

item.title: On the Multi-Weight Shift-Sum Iterative Decoding of Short BCH Codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates a shift-sum decoding algorithm that employs dual codewords. Existing dual codeword shift-sum decoding schemes mainly rely on minimum-weight dual codewords. However, the number of such codewords is often limited, which restricts the amount of reliability information available to the decoder. To address this issue, we extend the component counting mechanism from minimum-weight dual codewords to dual codewords whose Hamming weights lie within a prescribed upper bound. We further introduce a normalized component counting rule to suppress the overcounting bias caused by the much larger populations of higher-weight classes. Based on this framework, we develop a hard-decision iterative error reduction decoder and a soft information-aided iterative error reduction decoder. Numerical results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing minimum-weight shift-sum baselines especially for short codes where additional dual codeword information is particularly valuable.
item.dc:creator: Yinglei Yang, Di Zhang, Aimin Li, Yifei Shen, Alexey Frolov, Bo Gu

item.title: The Right to Be Forgotten under Correlation: Privacy-Utility Tradeoffs
item.description: arXiv:2610.17088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study privacy-preserving algorithms that redact information from a correlated dataset. The goal is to reduce the information leakage about sensitive parts. We analytically characterize the optimal tradeoff between privacy (leakage through correlation) and utility (number of redactions) for local mechanisms and binary Markovian correlations. Our result shows how to decompose the mechanism design problem into a sequence of local mechanism design problems and reveals their sequential relation. The optimal mechanism is the solution to a Finite-Horizon Deterministic Markov Decision Process.
item.dc:creator: Luis Massny, Rawad Bitar, Fangwei Ye, Salim El Rouayheb

item.title: Puncturing-inclusion constructions of optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes using semifield codes
item.description: arXiv:2610.17570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes are essential components of the multilevel construction of constant dimension codes for random network coding. This paper aims to construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes, focusing on the diagram \([3,3,3,5]\) with rank distance \(3\). We construct an optimal \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) Ferrers diagram rank-metric code for every prime power \(q\), thereby answering an open problem posed by Etzion et al. in 2016~\cite{Etzion2016}. The construction first builds a \([3\times4,4,3]_q\) MRD code and then proves that the Delsarte dual of its puncturing on the last column contains a \([3\times3,3,3]_q\) MRD code, which comes from semifield codes. We further construct optimal Ferrers diagram rank-metric codes for two infinite families of Ferrers diagrams: the first relies on the \([[3,3,3,5],6,3]_q\) construction and holds for every prime power \(q\), while the second is binary and obtained directly by the puncturing-inclusion construction.
item.dc:creator: Dengming Xu, Chengming Duan, Yong Jin, Yuhao Ning

item.title: Distribution-Dependent Improvements of McDiarmid's Inequality via R\'enyi Divergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.17736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether R\'enyi divergence can sharpen McDiarmid's inequality and its distribution-dependent refinement induced by KL divergence. Starting from Marton's transportation proof, we show that its transport inequality fails in general when KL divergence is replaced by R\'enyi divergence of order $0<\alpha<1$. For sums of independent bounded random variables, however, the additivity of R\'enyi divergence allows us to adapt the argument and derive concentration bounds. For Bernoulli sums, these bounds strictly improve on the distribution-dependent bound induced by KL divergence over a range of deviation thresholds. We also establish a distribution-dependent refinement of Gilardoni's inequality relating total variation to R\'enyi divergence, providing explicit constants for our general concentration bounds.
item.dc:creator: Amedeo Roberto Esposito, Adrien Vandenbroucque, Michael Gastpar

item.title: Learned Score-Based Turbo Message Passing for Channel Recovery From Spatially Compressed Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2610.17785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid beamforming (HBF) reduces the hardware cost of massive MIMO base stations, but its channel acquisition requires recovering the full spatial-domain channel from highly compressed beam-domain observations. This paper proposes a learned score-based turbo message passing (L-STMP) framework for uplink HBF channel recovery under extreme spatial compression. By deeply unfolding the turbo message-passing loop and introducing trainable calibration parameters and learnable score priors in each layer, L-STMP liberates STMP from the idealized compression-matrix requirements of right-rotational invariance, and reduces inference complexity to only several unfolded layers. In addition, to preserve dominant channel components that random discrete Fourier transform (DFT) selection may miss, we introduce precoding matrix indicator (PMI)-assisted beam selection as a low-overhead directional prior. Simulation results demonstrate that L-STMP consistently outperforms existing baselines and obtains substantial reconstruction gains under PMI-assisted compression in channel reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Yiming Wei, Xiaojun Yuan

item.title: The Covering Radius of the Reed--Muller Code RM(1,9) is 242
item.description: arXiv:2610.17871v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What is the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,9) ? This is a long-standing open problem in cryptography and coding theory. In this paper, we resolve this problem, and prove that the covering radius of RM(1,9) is 242. We exclude nonlinearity 244 by obtaining a cubic Boolean function achieving a sharp Walsh $\ell^1$ bound. Its equality cases reduce either to an impossible cubic hyperplane restriction or to two homogeneous cubic forms in the Brier--Langevin classification. To exclude nonlinearity 243, we deduce the inequality ${\Vert W_g\Vert }_{1}+2|W_g(0)|\le 10368$, and then reduce either to a spectrum bounded by 24 or to the same expression to be at least 10496.
item.dc:creator: Qichun Wang, Yueying Lou, Zifan Wang

item.title: The Maximum Nonlinearity of 8-variable Balanced Boolean Functions is 116
item.description: arXiv:2610.17897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does there exist an 8-variable balanced Boolean function with nonlinearity 118? This is a famous and long-standing open problem in Boolean functions. In this paper, we give a negative answer to this open problem, and prove that the maximum nonlinearity of balanced Boolean functions in 8 variables is 116, establishing the 8-variable instance of Dobbertin's conjectured recursion for the minimum Walsh peak of balanced functions. Equivalently, the covering radius of the Reed--Muller code RM(1,8) in 0-resilient Boolean functions is 116. We deduce the result by obtaining a quadratic form of polar rank 6, and reducing the problem to the existence of a 6-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity greater than 26 whose Hamming distance to a bent function is between 4 and 6.
item.dc:creator: Yueying Lou, Youle Xu, Qichun Wang

item.title: Routing Optimality for Demand Graphs of Matching Number at Most Two
item.description: arXiv:2610.17911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that network coding and fractional routing have the same capacity region in undirected networks whose demand graph has matching number at most two, that is, when no three demand edges have pairwise disjoint endpoints. The metric-packing reduction of Liu et al. reduces this problem to a distance-weighted communication inequality on the fixed graph $\Gamma_{3,3}$. We first prove two entropy inequalities for sessions between designated terminal pairs on $\Gamma_{3,3}$. We then extend this result to sessions with arbitrary endpoints to obtain the distance-weighted communication bound required by the reduction. The proof combines conditional entropy inequalities with two graph contractions and an information inequality for deterministic interaction. Combining this inequality with the existing reduction establishes routing optimality for this class of demand graphs.
item.dc:creator: Xiaohong Cai, Yulin Chen

item.title: Chordal Codes: Code Construction and Efficient Gaussian-Elimination Decoding
item.description: arXiv:2610.17934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maximum-likelihood decoding of linear codes over erasure channels can be considered as solving a linear system of a column submatrix of the parity-check matrix. In practice, Gaussian elimination is usually applied, and its computational cost depends on the structure of the matrix, especially the sparsity and the fill-in generated during the elimination. The \emph{chordal graph}, or \emph{triangulated graph}, first introduced by C. Berge, has a so-called \emph{perfect elimination ordering}, indicating that if the primal graph of a matrix is a chordal graph, then there exists a perfect elimination ordering such that a special class of fill-in under Gaussian elimination following this ordering will be avoided. In this paper, we introduce \emph{chordal codes}, i.e., codes equipped with parity-check matrices such that the primal graphs of the parity-check matrices are chordal. We prove that, for a chordal code, the decoding submatrix associated with any erasure pattern retains a chordal primal graph. So, the complexity of chordal elimination (Gaussian elimination following the perfect elimination ordering applied to the chordal code decoding) will be smaller than decoding a random code by Gaussian elimination. Also, we provide an upper bound on the complexity of chordal elimination.
item.dc:creator: Yulin Chen, Laigang Guo, Tong Li, Mingyang Zhu

item.title: Latency-Aware Uplink NOMA-MEC with PASS: A Feasibility-First Resource Allocation Framework
