item.dc:creator: Xinwei Yue, Xinglun Tao, Jingjing Zhao, Xianfu Lei, Yuanwei Liu, Zhiguo Ding

item.title: Reduced-Feedback Hybrid Precoding for Wideband mmWave MIMO-OFDM Systems via Hierarchical Interpolation
item.description: arXiv:2605.02418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a feedback-efficient hybrid precoding framework for wideband millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. To reduce the hardware cost of radio-frequency (RF) chains and the feedback burden associated with frequency-selective digital precoding, frequency-flat analog precoders and combiners are first constructed from the dominant angle-of-arrival (AoA) and angle-of-departure (AoD) directions associated with the strongest propagation paths. For digital precoding, a shared quantized codebook is designed using the Lloyd algorithm, and a binary-search-based hierarchical interpolation method is developed to identify codeword switching locations between adjacent pilot subcarriers. By avoiding exhaustive codeword comparisons over all intermediate subcarriers, the proposed method reduces online search complexity and enables compact digital-precoder feedback. For the considered system configuration, the proposed method achieves a worst-case feedback reduction of approximately 98.34% relative to full-grid per-subcarrier feedback. Simulation results further demonstrate competitive spectral efficiency and bit error rate (BER) performance, low computational cost, and robustness under imperfect effective channel state information (CSI).
item.dc:creator: Po-Heng Chou, Jia-Qing Lin, Wei-Chen Lin, Wan-Jen Huang, Ronald Y. Chang

item.title: An Improved Lower Bound on Support Size of Capacity-Achieving Inputs for the Binomial Channel: Extended version
item.description: arXiv:2605.12472v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the binomial channel and the structure of its capacity-achieving input and output distributions. It is known that the capacity-achieving input distribution is discrete and supported on finitely many points. The best previously known bounds show that the support size of the capacity-achieving distribution is lower-bounded by a term of order $\sqrt n$ and upper-bounded by a term of order $n/2$, where $n$ is the number of trials. In this work, we derive a new lower bound on the support size of order $\sqrt{n\log\log n}$, up to explicit constants. The proof consists of three main steps. First, we derive new upper and lower bounds on the capacity with a gap that vanishes as $n\to\infty$, which yields $C(n)=\frac12\log\frac{n\pi}{2e}+o(1)$. Second, we show that the Beta-binomial output distribution induced by the reference input $X_r\sim\mathrm{Beta}(1/2,1/2)$ is asymptotically optimal: it approaches the capacity-achieving output distribution in relative entropy and, after a comparison step, in $\chi^2$ divergence. Third, we prove a quantitative $\chi^2$ approximation lower bound showing that this Beta-binomial output cannot be approximated too well by the output induced by a $K$-point input. Combining these ingredients forces the capacity-achieving input distribution to have at least order $\sqrt{n\log\log n}$ mass points.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadamin Baniasadi, Antonino Favano, Luca Barletta, Alex Dytso

item.title: Secure Joint Source-Channel Coding of Multimodal Semantic Sources
item.description: arXiv:2605.14334v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of secure joint source-channel coding for multimodal semantic sources transmitted over noisy wiretap channels. The source model consists of $m$ modalities (e.g., image, audio, and sensor data), all represented as random variables. The encoder observes independent and identically distributed samples of an arbitrary non-empty subset of modalities, which are encoded, using wiretap coding with a help of a secret key shared with the legitimate receiver, and transmitted over a discrete memoryless wiretap channel. The legitimate receiver reconstructs all modalities. We extend the rate-distortion-perception characterisation to semantic unimodal and multimodal sources. We establish outer and inner bounds on the tradeoff between transmission rate, key rate, fidelity, and secrecy under per-modality distortion and perception constraints, and per-subset equivocation constraint. The bounds coincide for the less noisy wiretap channels. Our results show that the fundamental limit for secrecy consists of three operationally distinct components: the level of compression of each subset of modalities, the secret key rate, and the statistics of the wiretap channel.
item.dc:creator: Denis Kozlov, Mahtab Mirmohseni, Rahim Tafazolli

item.title: Learning from Totally Unpaired Data via Minimum Conditional Entropy Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2605.16229v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Consider an "unsupervised classification" setting, where the goal is to learn a predictor of the categorical class variable $X$ using the categorical feature variables $Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$, but we can only train the predictor on $m+1$ totally unpaired datasets, where each dataset only consists of unordered samples of one of the variables $X,Y_{1},\ldots,Y_{m}$. Although this problem is highly underdetermined, we demonstrate that, under the assumption that a predictor with small cross entropy loss exists, we can find a good predictor by coupling the marginal distributions of $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ in a manner that minimizes the conditional entropy $H(X|Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)$. This problem, which we call minimum conditional entropy coupling (MCEC), is a generalization of the widely studied minimum entropy coupling problem (where $m=1$). Although the MCEC problem is NP-hard, we give an algorithm with a time complexity that is polynomial in $N$, which gives a coupling with conditional entropy within $O(\log \log N)$ from the optimum, where $N$ is the dimension of the output coupling. We also evaluate the performance of the MCEC predictor on synthetic and real-world datasets.
item.dc:creator: Cheuk Ting Li, Jun Chen, Shahab Asoodeh

item.title: Performance of Planar XYZ and XZZX Codes under Homogeneous and Spatially Nonuniform Noise
item.description: arXiv:2605.23236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) decoder is a standard decoding strategy for surface codes, but its performance can degrade considerably under biased noise. In this work, a modified family of surface codes, termed the XYZ planar code, is introduced, and MWPM is extended to posterior MWPM (pMWPM), which exploits the information provided by mixed stabilizers with almost no increase in decoding complexity. The XYZ--pMWPM and XZZX code--decoder combinations are compared under homogeneous independent and identically distributed (IID) Pauli noise and processor-derived independent nonidentically distributed (INID) noise. Under homogeneous biased Pauli noise, pMWPM substantially increases the threshold of the XYZ planar code relative to conventional MWPM. At finite code distances, particularly for small codes under strong bias, XYZ--pMWPM achieves logical error rates comparable to or lower than those of XZZX. Under INID noise, the pseudothreshold ordering observed under the corresponding homogeneous IID references is not always preserved; in some hardware--distance settings, XYZ--pMWPM achieves pseudothresholds comparable to or higher than those of XZZX. Within XZZX, qubit-specific weighting consistently yields higher INID pseudothresholds than average-rate weighting for the hardware instances considered. It is further found that the IID--INID pseudothreshold shift depends strongly on the physical-error scalarization and the construction of the homogeneous IID reference. These results show that pMWPM efficiently exploits the mixed-stabilizer structure of the XYZ planar code and provides competitive finite-distance decoding under biased and spatially nonuniform noise.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwei Wang, Liqi Wang

item.title: Deriving Approximate Message Passing from the Convex Gaussian Min-Max Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2606.27769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Approximate message passing (AMP) provides fast iterative algorithms for high-dimensional signal recovery with Gaussian design matrices, while the Convex Gaussian Min--max Theorem (CGMT) gives a static optimization framework for obtaining sharp asymptotic characterizations of convex estimators. Although these two frameworks often lead to the same scalar state-evolution equations, their connection is usually indirect. In this paper, we establish a direct connection between the two for regularized linear regression in the proportional high-dimensional regime. When the CGMT Auxiliary Optimization (AO) and Primary Optimization (PO) give the same primal-dual solution, we show that the CGMT framework recovers the AMP fixed-point equations, including the Onsager correction. We further identify the AO Gaussian vectors with the Gaussian perturbations in the primal and residual AMP channels. For regularized $M$-estimation, the same viewpoint recovers the fixed point of scalar-variance max-sum Generalized AMP (GAMP). These results show that the AMP (and GAMP) fixed-point equations can be recovered from the CGMT framework and may suggest AMP-like algorithms in settings where standard derivations are unavailable.
item.dc:creator: Vikrant Malik, Babak Hassibi

item.title: Partial Path Interception in Derivation DAGs: Exact Reliability Laws and a Sharp Complexity Dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2608.11782v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce partial path interception on derivation DAGs (directed acyclic graphs), a combinatorial optimization problem arising from proof-valid caching: stored objects must be logical consequences of a premise base whose premises are erased independently, a query is recovered only while derivable from surviving premises and stored objects, and the queried object itself may not be stored, so reliability must come from premises or intermediate consequences. An exact residual-leaf law pins the recovery probability to a closed form in the exposed-leaf count and reduces design to weighted partial path interception (PPI) on the witness DAG. We classify PPI across its canonical regimes: it is NP-complete already on depth-two DAGs with leaf out-degree two and fixed-parameter intractable in the budget, ruling out efficient approximation schemes; it contains smallest T-edge subgraph as a special case, hence admits no approximation within the square root of the optimum under the Strongish Planted Clique Hypothesis, matched there by trivial leaf-only caching; whereas unique-path instances admit an exact dynamic program, bounded-treewidth instances are fixed-parameter tractable, and individual coverage admits a tight logarithmic greedy guarantee. Semantic-module caches are exactly optimal for shared workloads under exact module routing. An appendix prices transparency against a coded erasure benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Jianfeng Xu

item.title: Deterministic Identification over Additive Gaussian Channels
item.description: arXiv:2608.27243v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modern communication systems impose strict demands on data rate, reliability, and power efficiency. In this context, emerging communication paradigms such as identification via channels have become an important topic in post-Shannon information theory, offering the potential for substantially higher identification rates than in conventional channel coding.Deterministic identification is particularly interesting for specialized communication scenarios because it provides a balance between implementation complexity and the communication gains due to higher identification rates. It is therefore a promising communication scheme for future communication systems, including molecular communication systems. Additive Gaussian channels, particularly the additive white Gaussian channel, are among the most important channel models for analyzing the performance of communication systems in information and communication theory. This importance stems from both their mathematical tractability and their ubiquitous appearance in practical applications. To date the deterministic identification capacity for additive Gaussian channels remains unknown even for the simplest case of the additive white Gaussian channel. In this paper, we establish tight bounds on the deterministic identification capacity of additive Gaussian channels by introducing a new perspective on deterministic identification. To this end, we apply results from lattice theory to obtain new capacity results.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan E. W. Huffmann, Holger Boche

item.title: Embedding Linear Codes into Optimal Self-Orthogonal Codes Based on Constraint-Preserving Genetic Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2609.02135v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the problem of finding shortest self-orthogonal embeddings of a given code which have the largest possible minimum distance by employing a constraint-preserving genetic algorithm. We show that the orthogonal group is generated by transvections corresponding to weight-four vectors. Using this result together with the fact that all shortest self-orthogonal embeddings can be obtained through the action of the orthogonal group, we construct a genetic algorithm in which each chromosome is represented by a sequence of weight-four vectors. Applying our algorithm to codes with dimensions $9\le k\le 15$ and lengths $22\le n\le 256$, we obtain 280 inequivalent optimal self-orthogonal codes. In particular, we obtain 34 codes with new parameters and 100 codes which are inequivalent to previously known codes with the same parameters.
item.dc:creator: Haeun Lim, Junmin An, Jon-Lark Kim

item.title: Further results on binary linear covering codes and saturating sets in projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.16078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The binary length function $\ell_2(r,R)$ is the smallest length of a binary linear code with codimension (redundancy) $r$ and covering radius $R$. Let $s_2(N,\rho)$ be the smallest size of a $\rho$-saturating set in the binary projective space $\mathrm{PG}(N,2)$. It is known that the binary length function satisfies $\ell_2(r,R)=s_2(r-1,R-1)$. We obtain the following new upper bounds on $\ell_2(r,R)$, improving the previously known upper bounds by $\Delta(r,R)$: $R=2,r=2t\ge28$, and $r=10,18,20$, $\ell_2(r,2)=s_2(r-1,1)\le51\cdot2^{r/2-5}-1,\Delta(r,2)=2^{r/2-5}$; $R=3,r=3t-1\ge41$ and $r=26$, $\ell_2(r,3)=s_2(r-1,2)\le818\cdot2^{(r-26)/3}-1$, $\Delta(41,3)=63,\Delta(r,3)=2^{(r-26)/3}$ if $r\ge44$. To obtain these bounds, we construct new infinite code families, using distinct versions of the $q^m$-concatenating constructions of covering codes, including new versions proposed in this paper. We also obtain new useful partitions of column sets of parity check matrices of some codes. The new code families provide the asymptotic covering-density bounds $\overline{\mu}(2)\le2601/2048<1.27002$, $\overline{\mu}(3)\le1.35935$, improving the previously known bounds and giving rise to the new upper bounds $f(2)\le2601/2048<1.27002$, $f(3)\le1.35935$ on the constants $f(2),f(3)$ of the Green's Open Problem 40.
item.dc:creator: Alexander A. Davydov, Stefano Marcugini, Fernanda Pambianco, Stephen Wu

item.title: Fourier Ratio and Restricted Isometry via Entropic Descent
item.description: arXiv:2609.22568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this second paper on descent methods as proof mechanisms in harmonic analysis (the first treated Bourgain's $\Lambda(p)$ selection theorem), entropic mirror descent gives an improved restricted isometry bound, improving sampling and recovery bounds in the Fourier Ratio program. Let $H$ be a complex $n\times n$ matrix with $H^*H=nI$ and $|H_{ij}|=1$. For fixed $0<\varepsilon<\frac14$ and $A_0>0$, independent Bernoulli row selection with expected cardinality $C_{\varepsilon,A_0}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log(2r)\leq m\leq n/2$ preserves, after normalization by $\sqrt m$, the squared norm of every complex vector $y$ with $\|y\|_1\leq\sqrt r\|y\|_2$ within a factor $1\pm\varepsilon$, with failure probability at most $Cn^{-A_0}$. This includes every $r$-sparse vector and also fully supported ones; support size enters only through this inequality. For $y=\widehat f$ the condition is exactly $\operatorname{FR}(f)^2\leq r$, where $\operatorname{FR}(f)=\|\widehat f\|_1/\|\widehat f\|_2$, giving uniform energy sampling and approximate recovery even for signals with full Fourier support. The same holds for a uniform subset of prescribed cardinality, and for discrete Fourier and real Hadamard matrices. At fixed accuracy the bound removes one sparsity logarithm from the earlier count and replaces $\log n$ by $\log\frac{2en}{r}$; for Walsh matrices it matches, up to constants, the lower bound of B\l asiok et al.\ in their range. One relative-entropy potential controls the corrections of an amplitude predictor at every scale; counting them on the symmetric difference of two samples gives the uniform estimate. We also prove the sufficient bound $C_{A_0}\varepsilon^{-5}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log\frac{2r}{\varepsilon}$, and stable sparse recovery from $Cs\log\frac{2en}{s}\log(2s)$ measurements, with error controlled by the noise and the best $s$-term approximation.
item.dc:creator: W. Burstein, A. Iosevich, B. Krause

item.title: Affine Symmetries of Polynomial Roots with Multiplicities and Applications to Constacyclic Codes
item.description: arXiv:2609.26414v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f(X)$ be a polynomial over a finite field, and let its defining function record the multiplicities of its roots. In this paper, we introduce the affine stabilizer group and the affine stabilizer group scheme of the defining function of $f(X)$. These objects characterize the affine symmetries of the roots of $f(X)$ together with their multiplicities. We establish structural descriptions of these affine stabilizers and relate them to the coefficient structure of $f(X)$. In particular, the affine stabilizer group determines quotient structures of the defining function, which yield canonical descriptions of the corresponding semi-invariant polynomial spaces. The resulting coefficient constraints provide explicit restrictions on the possible supports of polynomials with prescribed affine symmetries. The affine stabilizer group scheme further captures infinitesimal symmetries arising from multiple roots and gives refined coefficient constraints beyond those obtained from ordinary affine transformations. We apply this framework to generator polynomials of constacyclic codes over finite fields. The affine stabilizer structure of a generator polynomial induces subcodes defined by semi-invariant conditions and provides constraints on their dimensions and Hamming distances. In the special case of multiplicative symmetries, the construction specializes to the support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes.
item.dc:creator: Li Zhu, Hongfeng Wu

item.title: Fully 3GPP-Compatible Long-Range Sensing for LEO-ISAC: A Window-Grid Processing Framework
item.description: arXiv:2609.30653v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses long-range sensing in bistatic low-Earth-orbit integrated sensing and communication (LEO-ISAC). Conventional OFDM sensing fails in LEO-ISAC because millisecond-scale propagation delays destroy the transmitter--receiver symbol alignment and, with multiple targets, make the receive window longer than the transmitted block. We propose a window-grid (WG) processing framework that exploits the known beam-intersection swath to resolve both problems purely at the receiver, leaving the transmitted 3GPP OFDM waveform unmodified: the swath delay span is folded into cyclic-prefix-sized slices, each handled by one WG. With 100.8 MHz bandwidth at bistatic ranges beyond 640 km, simulations demonstrate meter-level ranging of two targets, and Monte-Carlo trials over random target--satellite geometries show that, with an ephemeris-based satellite-selection rule, every target is detected with a 90th-percentile range error of 2.4 m.
item.dc:creator: Yi Geng, Xun Fan, Chenfeng Xu, Yu Zhao

item.title: Recovery Set Structures and Service Rates of Codes Obtained by the Plotkin-type Construction
item.description: arXiv:2610.01900v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In distributed storage systems, redundancy enables a single data object to be reconstructed using several disjoint groups of servers. The resulting service rate region (SRR) captures all combinations of object request rates that the system can support simultaneously without overloading any individual server. We analyze the SRR of binary codes obtained via the Plotkin-type construction. We demonstrate that each recovery set for an information object of the Plotkin-type code $\mathcal{C}_p$ induces a corresponding recovery set for the same data object characterized by the underlying code $\mathcal{C}$. Furthermore, by characterizing the recovery sets structure of $\mathcal{C}_p$ in terms of the recovery set structure of $\mathcal{C}$, we identify the additional recovery sets introduced by this construction. Using the associated recovery hypergraphs, we establish bounds on the SRRs of $\mathcal{C}_p$ and iterated code $\mathcal{C}_{p^m}$ in terms of the SRR of $\mathcal{C}$. We consider the family of first-order binary Reed-Muller codes and show how the recovery structure, and consequently, the service rates of R$(1,m)$ for arbitrary $m$ can be recursively derived from a generator matrix of R$(1,2)$ through our results for successive Plotkin-type constructions.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka Choudhary, Maheshanand Bhaintwal

item.title: Cold-Atom Rydberg Array with Spatiotemporal Multiplexing for High-Sensitivity Wireless Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.07642v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An effective Cold-Atom Rydberg Array (CoRA) architecture is investigated, which addresses the fundamental thermal noise limit in classical electromagnetics and intrinsic Doppler broadening as well as photon shot noise in conventional hot-vapor cell-based atomic receivers. However, translating the CoRA-based quantum electrometers into practical wireless communication receivers is bottlenecked by both the macroscopic readout dead-times and nonlinear binomial population counts rather than the additive-Gaussian baseband samples in conventional receivers. To address these critical challenges and facilitate the practicality of the CoRA, in this paper, a subarray scheduling-based spatiotemporal multiplexing (STM) framework is first proposed for gap-free symbol interrogation within an admitted packet. Additionally, a signal detection scheme based on a joint binomial particle smoother (JBPS) is proposed for burst-wise state and data inference. Furthermore, the weak-signal quantum-projection-noise (QPN) limit and the state-averaged finite-alphabet rate are derived for CoRA-assisted wireless communications. Numerical results demonstrate that: 1) The proposed STM-based CoRA scheme resolves the macroscopic temporal bottleneck for continuous signal sampling; 2) The proposed JBPS approach effectively mitigates the nonlinear noise amplification to achieve a lower bit error rate; and 3) Performance analysis reveals a fundamental sensitivity-sustainability tradeoff that increasing the number of atoms effectively suppresses the QPN, but simultaneously reduces the sustainable packet repetition rate.
item.dc:creator: Jian Xiao, Tierui Gong, Chau Yuen

item.title: Markovian Continuity of the MMSE
item.description: arXiv:2504.14659v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Minimum mean square error (MMSE) estimation is widely used in signal processing, information theory, and related fields. Despite its practical robustness, the MMSE can be discontinuous under standard notions of stochastic convergence. To bridge this gap, we review classical counterexamples to the continuity of the MMSE and identify two obstructions: failure of second-moment convergence and approximating observations carrying more information about the limit estimand than the limit observation does. Motivated by practical acquisition mechanisms, we study MMSE continuity under two natural constraints: (1) continuity of the second moment, and (2) a degradedness (Markov) restriction ensuring that each approximating observation is no more informative than the limit observation is about the limit estimand. Under these conditions, we establish continuity of the MMSE and of the MMSE estimator. We provide complementary semicontinuity results and continuity guarantees in related settings and establish continuity under linear estimation. We further extend the analysis to the families of Bregman divergences and continuous metric and generalized metric cost functions, including the Kullback-Leibler and Jensen-Shannon divergences as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Elad Domanovitz, Anatoly Khina

item.title: LiDAL-Assisted RLNC-NOMA in OWC Systems
item.description: arXiv:2504.16498v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optical wireless communication (OWC) is a key enabler for immersive indoor data transmission in future wireless networks. However, managing multi-user interference remains challenging in dense indoor OWC deployments with multiple optical access points (APs) serving multiple users. In this paper, we propose a dual-function OWC system for communication and localization. For data transmission, we design non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) combined with random linear network coding (RLNC): NOMA serves multiple users simultaneously via power-domain multiplexing, while RLNC improves decoding robustness under residual noise and processing impairments. The system is assisted by a light detection and localization (LiDAL) module that estimates users' spatio-temporal presence and location to enable dynamic user association. LiDAL also supports channel state information (CSI) estimation in realistic indoor scenarios where CSI may be noisy and/or highly correlated. We evaluate RLNC-NOMA by analyzing the probability of successful decoding and comparing it with conventional NOMA and orthogonal schemes. In addition, we derive the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) to evaluate the localization accuracy. The results indicate that RLNC-NOMA increases the probability of successful decoding, and that the proposed unbiased location estimator achieves 44% better CSI accuracy than the baseline CSI estimation and improves the overall system performance.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed A. Hassan, Ahmad Adnan Qidan, Taisir Elgorashi, Jaafar Elmirghani

item.title: MIRANDA: short signatures from a leakage-free full-domain-hash scheme
item.description: arXiv:2510.07479v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present $\mathsf{Miranda}$, the first family of full-domain-hash signatures based on matrix codes. This signature scheme fulfils the paradigm of Gentry, Peikert and Vaikuntanathan ($\mathsf{GPV}$), which gives strong security guarantees. Our trapdoor is very simple and generic: if we propose it with matrix codes, it can actually be instantiated in many other ways since it only involves a subcode of a decodable code (or lattice) in a unique decoding regime of parameters. Though $\mathsf{Miranda}$ signing algorithm relies on a decoding task where there is exactly one solution, there are many possible signatures given a message to sign and we ensure that signatures are not leaking information on their underlying trapdoor by means of a very simple procedure involving the drawing of a small number of uniform bits. In particular $\mathsf{Miranda}$ does not use a rejection sampling procedure which makes its implementation a very simple task contrary to other $\mathsf{GPV}$-like signatures schemes such as $\mathsf{Falcon}$ or even $\mathsf{Wave}$. We instantiate $\mathsf{Miranda}$ with the famous family of Gabidulin codes represented as spaces of matrices and we study thoroughly its security (in the EUF-CMA security model). For~$128$ bits of classical security, the signature sizes are as low as~$90$ bytes and the public key sizes are in the order of~$2.6$ megabytes.
item.dc:creator: Alain Couvreur, Thomas Debris-Alazard, Philippe Gaborit, Adrien Vin\c{c}otte

item.title: Quantum Voting Protocol for Centralized and Distributed Voting Based on Phase-Flip Counting
item.description: arXiv:2510.15243v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a quantum voting protocol that uses superposition and entanglement to enable anonymous voting with trusted voting machines, in a centralized setting with a single machine and in a distributed setting where several machines are linked to a voting center through quantum channels. A voter selects a candidate through a restricted ballot interface; the machine encodes the vote as a phase-flip operation, controlled by the voter's identity register, on an entangled candidate state. Tallying is performed by interference with a reference branch followed by a measurement of the candidate register, which reproduces the vote distribution without iterative classical counting. Because every tallying run consumes the quantum state, the machines store the cast choices classically and replay the voting stage for each run. The protocol uses only basic quantum gates (Hadamard and controlled-Z). We provide analytical examples (4 voters with 2 candidates and 8 voters with 3 candidates) and numerical experiments that simulate ideal conditions, depolarizing, memory, readout, and gate noise, faulty or mistaken ballots, larger instances with confidence intervals, and sampling convergence. The simulations reproduce the theoretical tally probabilities in the ideal case and show how the tally is distorted by noise and by faulty ballots; no error correction or mitigation is applied. Voter anonymity is formalized as the indistinguishability of tallying transcripts under vote permutations, and an identity-dephasing step renders the identity register exactly maximally mixed under the stated trust assumptions. The numbers of protocol runs needed for exact tallying and for winner identification are analyzed explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Ali Emre Aydin, Ammar Daskin

item.title: Short Blocks, Fast Sensing: Finite Blocklength Tradeoffs in RIS-Assisted ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2511.02673v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is a cornerstone for future sixth-generation (6G) networks, enabling simultaneous connectivity and environmental awareness. However, practical realization faces significant challenges, including residual self-interference (SI) in full-duplex (FD) systems and performance degradation of short-packet transmissions under finite blocklength (FBL) constraints. This work studies a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted FD ISAC system serving multiple downlink users while tracking a moving target, explicitly accounting for SI and FBL effects in both communication and sensing. We formulate an optimization framework to minimize service adaptation gaps while ensuring sensing reliability, solved via alternating optimization and successive convex approximation. Numerical results show that short blocklengths enable fast adaptation but increase radar outage due to fewer pulses and motion sensitivity, whereas longer blocklengths improve SINR and reduce outages but allow target motion to degrade sensing. A regime-dependent "sweet spot" emerges, where blocklength and beamformer allocation jointly balance throughput and sensing, with HD favored at very short blocklengths and FD at longer blocklengths. RIS-assisted optimization expands the FD-operating regime, enabling reliable communication and radar sensing at lower blocklengths.
item.dc:creator: Adam Umra, Kevin Weinberger, Aymen Khaleel, Gerald Enzner, Aydin Sezgin

item.title: Frobenius Revivals in Laplacian Cellular Automata: Replication, Entropy, and Information Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2511.17389v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate Frobenius revivals in prime-modulus Laplacian cellular automata. The Frobenius identity yields exact superpositions of translated, coefficient-weighted seed copies at prime-power times; we distinguish this algebraic replication from their geometric separation. We investigate seed recovery from separated replicas and evaluate the correction of independent symbol errors introduced during transmission of encoded configurations. For the diagonal neighborhood, we determine the exact periods of moving corner operators on square windows and establish sufficient conditions for recovering any binary seed under a binary--ternary--binary schedule. The results connect prime-power algebraic structure with spatial pattern formation and precisely delimited forms of information recovery.
item.dc:creator: Ma{\l}gorzata Nowak-K\k{e}pczyk

item.title: Coherent Information Deletion: Bayesian, Generalized Bayesian and Possibilistic Unlearning
item.description: arXiv:2602.09061v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bayes' theorem admits an information processing interpretation due to Zellner (1988): under the Shannon information criterion, the posterior is the unique rule that processes prior and data information without information loss. We revisit these ideas from the perspective of information deletion. Given a posterior based on a complete dataset, what distribution should replace it when a subset of the data is removed? For ordinary Bayesian inference, we show that the corresponding information deletion objective is uniquely minimized by the leave-data-out posterior. We then extend the framework beyond likelihood-based inference from Bayes to the generalized Bayesian updating of Bissiri et al.(2016} based on loss functions. Requiring deletion to be coherent under sequential removal of loss contributions yields a deletion rule that exactly recovers the generalized posterior based only on the retained information. We further develop an axiomatic theory, beyond probabilistic inference, for possibilistic deletion and show that the same information-deletion perspective leads to a principled rule for exact possibilistic unlearning. Finally, restricting these exact deletion principles to tractable families leads naturally to variational Bayesian, generalized Bayesian, and maxitive possibilistic unlearning.
item.dc:creator: Hans Montcho, H{\aa}vard Rue, Maurizio Filippone

item.title: Convexity Meets Curvature: Lifted Near-Field Super-Resolution
item.description: arXiv:2602.14063v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Extra-large apertures, high carrier frequencies, and integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) are pushing array processing into the Fresnel region, where spherical wavefronts induce a range-dependent phase across the aperture. This curvature breaks the Fourier/Vandermonde structure behind classical subspace methods, and it is especially limiting with hybrid front-ends that provide only a small number of pilot measurements. Consequently, practical systems need continuous angle resolution and joint angle-range inference where many near-field approaches still rely on costly 2D gridding. We show that convexity can meet curvature via a lifted, gridless superresolution framework for near-field measurements. The key is a Bessel-Vandermonde factorization of the Fresnel-phase manifold that exposes a hidden Vandermonde structure in angle while isolating the range dependence into a compact coefficient map. Building on this, we introduce a lifting that maps each range bin and continuous angle to a structured rank-one atom, converting the nonlinear near-field model into a linear inverse problem over a row-sparse matrix. Recovery is posed as atomic-norm minimization and an explicit dual characterization via bounded trigonometric polynomials yields certificate-based localization that super-resolves off-grid angles and identifies active range bins. Simulations with strongly undersampled hybrid observations validate reliable joint angle-range recovery for next-generation wireless and ISAC systems.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Daei, G\'abor Fodor, Mikael Skoglund

item.title: Joint Communication and Sensing Security in MIMO-OFDM ISAC Systems via Artificial Noise and Ghosts
item.description: arXiv:2602.20045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables efficient sharing of wireless resources to support emerging applications, but it also introduces new sensing-based security vulnerabilities. Here, potential communication security threats include confidential messages intended for legitimate users being intercepted, and unauthorized receivers (Eves) passively exploiting target echoes to infer sensing parameters without users being aware. Despite these risks, the joint protection of sensing and communication security in ISAC systems remains unexplored. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a dual-secure ISAC framework that simultaneously protects sensing and communication against passive sensing Eves and communication Eves, without requiring their channel state information (CSI). Specifically, transmit beamformers are jointly designed to inject artificial noise (AN) to introduce interference to communication Eves, while deliberately distorting the reference signal available to sensing Eves to impair their sensing capability. Furthermore, the proposed design generates artificial ghosts (AGs) with fake angle-delay-Doppler profiles. The legitimate sensing receiver can suppress these AGs using its prior knowledge of the true target directions, whereas sensing Eves cannot, thereby significantly reducing their probability of correctly detecting the true targets. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively enhances both communication and sensing security, while preserving the performance of communication users and legitimate sensing receivers.
item.dc:creator: Yinchao Yang, Prabhat Raj Gautam, Yathreb Bouazizi, Mohammad Kazemi, Michael Breza, Julie A. McCann

item.title: Asymptotically good bosonic Fock state codes
item.description: arXiv:2603.15190v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the error-correction properties of multi-mode Fock-state codes under amplitude-damping (AD) noise, focusing on the asymptotic regime in which the total excitation of the code states grows without limit and the number of photon losses induced by the noise scales linearly with it. In this setting, existing code families, which correct only sublinearly many photon losses, do not protect against amplitude-damping (AD) noise with a constant loss parameter. As our main result, we address this gap by constructing asymptotically good Fock-state codes relying on random classical codes in the discrete simplex. Unlike many standard constructions of random quantum codes, our construction introduces randomness through the underlying classical indexing structure. Randomization also enables another desirable feature: bounded per-mode occupancy, which limits the number of photons in any individual mode and thereby increases the coherence lifetime of the code states. Finally, via a relation between Fock-state codes and permutation-invariant codes, our results also yield asymptotically good families of qudit permutation-invariant codes as well as codes in monolithic nuclear state spaces.
item.dc:creator: Dor Elimelech, Arda Aydin, Alexander Barg

item.title: Adaptive Patching Is Harder Than It Looks For Time-Series Forecasting
item.description: arXiv:2606.04074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Adaptive patching has been proposed for time-series forecasting: allocate finer patches where the sequence looks locally informative. We compare three adaptive patching methods with tuned uniform counterparts that use one fixed patch size throughout the input, while preserving each method's backbone family and shared training protocol. Across the evaluated long-horizon benchmarks, we observe mostly small accuracy differences and no consistent advantage for adaptive patching; uniform variants generally train faster and avoid adaptive routing at inference. Motivated by these observations, we develop a theoretical framework for budgeted patch allocation through a common resolution-density representation of uniform, nonuniform, and overlapping layouts, independently of the patching rule. Within a separable shared-loss model, we derive an exact criterion for when nonuniform allocation improves on uniform allocation at the same budget. We characterize modeled gains locally through a quadratic surrogate and bound them globally under strong convexity and a bounded loss derivative. The analysis distinguishes where resolution is placed from how much it is redistributed: even an allocation that correctly ranks regions by their weights can redistribute too much resolution and increase modeled loss. Without coupling across time, positive regional weights preserve the minimizers of the shared loss. When the shared loss has a common minimizing rate, the remaining absolute headroom for improvement tends to zero as the uniform rate approaches it. These results characterize the roles of regional weighting, placement, and redistribution strength under the stated model. The empirical findings support evaluating adaptive patching against a tuned uniform baseline and weighing any accuracy gain against the additional training and inference cost of adaptive routing.
item.dc:creator: Federico Zucchi, Yi Xie, Chao Zhang, Thomas Lampert, Ziyue Li

item.title: Dual-Security for Indoor OFDM-ISAC Systems via Temporal Artificial Noise
item.description: arXiv:2607.15710v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the rapid development of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) as a key enabler for future wireless networks, ensuring the security of both communication and sensing functions has become increasingly important. Current secure ISAC studies focus restrictively either on the communication or the sensing security, but not both. To bridge this gap, this paper investigates security for both, i.e., dual-security, in indoor orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based ISAC systems. Specifically, we consider a scenario in which a sensing user (SU) is authorized for sensing but may eavesdrop on communication data, while a communication user (CU) is authorized for communication but may perform unauthorized sensing. We chose this scenario as the pathological case where an authorized eavesdropper has more information and is more effective than an unauthorized one. To address this case, we propose the use of temporal artificial noise (AN) to prevent malicious CU sensing by enlarging its time-domain sensing error, and simultaneously degrade SU data eavesdropping by reducing its frequency-domain signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) with standard OFDM receiver processing. Meanwhile, our proposed scheme guarantees the sensing performance of the SU and the communication performance of the CU. We present numerical results that demonstrate AN can effectively provide dual protection for sensing and communication in OFDM-ISAC systems while guaranteeing the performance of legitimate users.
item.dc:creator: Yinchao Yang, Yathreb Bouazizi, Prabhat Raj Gautam, Michael Breza, Julie A. McCann

item.title: An Algebraic Framework for Data Systems: Classification and Optimization of Algebraic Structures for Data Organization and Coding
item.description: arXiv:2609.00273v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modern data systems are commonly studied through computational and information-theoretic methods, while their algebraic properties remain largely unexplored. This paper introduces a mathematical framework for modelling data systems using algebraic codes over finite groups, organized by an \emph{axiom signature}: each algebraic axiom of the data domain is shown to be \emph{sufficient} for a specific coding-theoretic capability, and each implication is given its precise reading (MDS parameters do not require a field; quotients require normality, not commutativity). Three types of results are presented. Proved: a Gilbert-Varshamov existence bound over arbitrary finite groups, commutative or not; explicit direct-sum codes over the elementary divisors of any finite abelian group; that transactions preserving a validity predicate form a submonoid of the full transformation monoid, which is not a group; that schema-preserving transformations form a finite group whose orbits are counted by Burnside's lemma; and that the constraint-preserving bijections of a data system form a finite group whose orbits partition the valid configurations. Demonstrated: an explicit code construction over $\mathbb{F}_5$, with known codes over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $(2^U,\triangle)$ cited to situate the framework. Proposed: an encoding efficiency measure Ef and an optimization functional $\Phi$ with tunable weights, both evaluated at declared coding instances. Weight-independent comparison holds under componentwise dominance; in general the weight simplex decomposes into polyhedral chambers on which the induced order is constant.
item.dc:creator: Kendy Inoa

item.title: Federated multiple testing with quantized p-values under family-wise error control
item.description: arXiv:2609.19708v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Several institutions test one family of hypotheses under family-wise error control but cannot pool their data, so each site releases only a quantized report of its p-value for each hypothesis, such as whether the p-value is significant. The report's resolution is the number of values it can take. We quantify the power lost to such reports relative to the most powerful centralized procedure given all p-values (the oracle), with reports and combining rule chosen optimally. A report from which the p-value can be recovered loses no power, so the loss is due to compression, not decentralization. Under the stated regularity and power-objective conditions, every finite resolution loses power, and the optimal loss decays as the inverse square of the resolution: equal-width intervals attain this order, and no partition into as many cells improves it. In two-site Beta examples, optimized one-bit reports are nearly lossless for a single hypothesis but lose several times as much power for two. At level 0.05 with two Beta(1,2) hypotheses, optimally combined three-bit equal-width reports retain 99.2% of oracle power. We give the power-optimal combining rule for given reports, and a rule using only their exactly known null distribution, valid under arbitrary dependence across hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Prasanjit Dubey, Xiaoming Huo

item.title: Monotonicity of the R\'enyi channel capacity under non-signaling assisted channel simulation
item.description: arXiv:2609.34213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an alternative variational proof that non-signaling correlations shared between the sender and receiver cannot increase the R\'enyi capacity of a classical channel. This monotonicity follows from the data-processing inequality for channel divergences established by Oufkir, Yao and Berta. Our approach works directly with the information-radius representation of the capacity. The constraints defining non-signaling boxes are linear in the box, while the R\'enyi capacity depends on the channel nonlinearly. We use a Legendre transform to express the capacity as an extremum over a family of affine functionals in which the channel appears linearly. Combining this method with separate arguments for the Shannon capacity and endpoint orders, we recover monotonicity at every order from zero to infinity. We then derive consequences for standard coding exponent functions: non-signaling simulation cannot increase the random-coding or sphere-packing exponent below capacity, or decrease the strong-converse exponent above capacity.
item.dc:creator: Tina Shariat, Matt Hoogsteder-Riera, Marco Tomamichel

item.title: On the signaling dimension of the cross-polytope
item.description: arXiv:2610.05924v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the general probabilistic model of information theory, the signaling dimension of a given communication protocol (or, equivalently, of its state space) is the smallest possible complexity of a classical communication protocol capable of perfectly simulating the given one in terms of input-output correlations. The signaling dimensions of three-, four-, and five-dimensional cross-polytopes have been known to be 3. We give logarithmic lower and upper bounds for the signaling dimensions of higher dimensional cross-polytopes, pinning down the value up to an additive gap of 2. The lower bound shows that the signaling dimension goes to infinity, in contrast to the case of balls and hypercubes.
item.dc:creator: Tam\'as Bencze, P\'eter E. Frenkel

item.title: Recovery Guarantees for Posterior Sampling of One-Bit Compressed Sensing
item.description: arXiv:2610.11834v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the sample complexity of noisy one-bit compressed sensing for signals drawn from a prior distribution. By characterizing the effective distributional complexity of the prior via its approximate covering number, we prove that posterior sampling achieves accurate recovery with high probability when the number of measurements scales with the logarithm of the approximate covering number, up to a one-bit separation gap factor. This upper bound is robust to learned prior mismatch. Specifically, we show that posterior sampling with an approximate prior remains reliable, provided that the learned prior distribution is sufficiently close to the true signal distribution in Wasserstein distance. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound for any reliable method of noisy one-bit compressed sensing, showing that our upper bound is nearly matched in its main prior dependent term. To approximate the ideal posterior sampling process for real world scenarios, we instantiate posterior sampling through a plug-and-play algorithm with diffusion priors. Experiments on the FFHQ and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach.
item.dc:creator: Jing Ma, Yujia Wu, Zhaoqiang Liu
